README.md 9 KB

SEOS report style: hand-off package, version 1

For Dan (SEOS / APEX), from James's team, 2026-10-12.

What this is

Our SEO report, made into a fixed procedure that SEOS can run for any business. From SEOS's own answers about one business (GET /businesses/{id}, /full-audit-result, /website-audit-result) and one small settings file, one command writes two documents:

  • Competitor Analysis: the Sales view, safe to send to the client.
  • Action Plan: the Service view, the team's working list.

No person and no AI writes anything at build time. Every sentence is a fixed template filled from the data, and rules decide the order (losing first, winning last), each status, and what is held back from the client. The same answers give the same documents, byte for byte, every time; the conformance test below proves it on Green Haven Industries (SEOS business 48), whose real answers, scrubbed, are the test fixture.

Start here

Needs Node 24. No npm packages. Chrome only for the optional browser checks.

# 1. The proof: rebuild Green Haven from its SEOS answers and compare with the expected files, byte for byte (about 3 s)
node conformance/conformance.mjs --no-browser
#    -> CONFORMANCE: PASS (...)        (drop --no-browser to add 46 checks in headless Chrome, about 17 s)

# 2. A run you can open: writes the two documents, the map file, the model and a run log into a new folder
node run-report.mjs --data=fixtures/green-haven-48/input --settings=fixtures/green-haven-48/settings.json \
  --extra-sweep=fixtures/green-haven-48/input/extra-ee/eagleeyes-scan-320-weed-near-me.json \
  --out=<new folder> --no-browser

Step 2's documents match fixtures/green-haven-48/expected/ byte for byte. Its market.json and report-data.json need not: the Eagle Eyes export's file time is stamped into them (OPEN-ITEMS M13), and unzipping may change it; and without --facts, meta.facts_check is null. Step 1 is the byte-for-byte proof: it pins the file time and passes --facts.

Then read, in this order:

  1. SPEC.md sections 1, 2 and 12: what it promises, the chain, and the recommended way into SEOS (run it as it is, accept it by the conformance test, port later only if wanted).
  2. OPEN-ITEMS.md sections 0 and 1: what is decided on our side, and what is on SEOS's side.
  3. The contract files when you need the detail.

Contract checks

Run from this folder.

E=fixtures/green-haven-48/expected
node contract/validate-model.mjs contract/report-data.schema.json $E/report-data.json --plant
node contract/validate-model.mjs contract/business-settings.schema.json fixtures/green-haven-48/settings.json
node contract/check-rules.mjs $E/report-data.json --rules=contract/rules.json --md=contract/RULES.md \
  --client-doc=$E/competitor-analysis.html --service-doc=$E/action-plan.html
node contract/check-outline.mjs contract/outline.json $E/competitor-analysis.html $E/action-plan.html --wording=contract/wording.json
node contract/check-wording.mjs contract/wording.json $E/report-data.json $E/competitor-analysis.html $E/action-plan.html --src=reference
node fixtures/green-haven-48/variants/run-variants.mjs

The last command rebuilds VARIANTS.md and fixtures/green-haven-48/variants/results.json in place (about 25 s); they must come out byte-identical (compare their sha256 before and after). Its runs go to a new folder under the system temp folder (about 13 MB); --work=<folder> puts them elsewhere.

Privacy

  • The fixture is a real client's data, scrubbed. Removed or emptied: another account's Google Analytics and Search Console readings (their request and result), tables and columns named for tokens, credentials or account links, the SEOS console users' e-mail addresses (replaced by person-<n>@example.invalid), the Eagle Eyes scan machine's network address and provider, and the location rows the chain does not read. input/SCRUBBED.md gives every count. Keep the package private: not in a public repository, not on a public host.
  • The Action Plan is a team document. It names our other accounts nowhere, but it carries everything else.
  • Other files here do name our other accounts and say they are ours: VARIANTS.md, fixtures/green-haven-48/variants/results.json and expected/report-data.json (the own-accounts check and its hold: three businesses on Green Haven's map, with their SEOS business ids, one of them its number 1 for "weed near me"); and, by website, the two accounts whose readings were emptied (expected/report-data.json, expected/market.json, the fixture's input, parts/A-build.json). Only a built Competitor Analysis may ever reach a client; never forward any other file of this package.
  • No key, token or password is in the package: a scan for the SEOS API key and the preview password found none, and a scan for the values of the other accounts' emptied readings found none.

Specification

The chain, the contract, determinism, how SEOS takes it on

SPEC.md 32 KB

SEOS report style: the specification

Version 1, 2026-10-12. Worked example and test fixture: Green Haven Industries, Elizabeth NJ (SEOS business 48), built from SEOS's answers fetched on 2026-10-12. Everything below was read from the reference code in reference/ or measured by running it; section 14 lists the runs.

1. What this package promises

From SEOS's own answers about one business, plus one small settings file, run-report.mjs writes two documents:

DocumentWhat it isBuilt with
Competitor AnalysisThe Sales view alone. Client-safe: nothing of the team's side is in the file.build-report.mjs --audience=client --doc="Competitor Analysis"
Action PlanThe Service view alone. The team's working document: every check, task and hold, minus anything about our other accounts.build-report.mjs --audience=service --doc="Action Plan"
  • No person and no AI writes anything at build time. Every sentence is a fixed template whose slots are filled from the data. Rules pick which template, the order, each status and what is held back from the client.
  • Same answers and same settings give the same bytes. market.json and both documents are byte-identical from run to run; report-data.json is equal apart from meta.built_at, the one clock read, which no document prints. One more input counts when an Eagle Eyes export is folded in: its file time, which reaches market.json and the model, never the documents (OPEN-ITEMS M13). Section 10 says what makes this hold and how it was shown.
  • Other data gives other documents by the same rules. More or fewer searches, rivals, directories or readings change the content, never the method. Missing or doubtful data is said plainly ("Not measured", "could not be read", or a number on hold that the client never sees) instead of guessed. Gaps remain, each listed in OPEN-ITEMS.md: some sentences carry Green Haven's facts or state a fact the code does not read (section 2), and data missing in certain ways crashes a stage or prints a wrong line (section 4).

2. The chain

SEOS API, saved as files                     settings.json (one per business)      Eagle Eyes scan export(s), optional
  business-<id>.json                                   |                            (a stopgap until SEOS sweeps every
  full-audit-<id>.json                                 |                             expected search itself)
  website-audit-<id>.json                              |                                   |
  engine_sweeps-all.json   (optional)                  |                       ee-scan-to-seos.mjs: SEOS sweep rows
  locations-all.json       (optional)                  |                       merge-sweep.mjs: a copy of the answers
        |                                              |                                   |   with those rows added
        +----------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                     |
  1. sweeps-market.mjs   -> market.json        the map file: each sweep's points, field, leaders, far rows, velocity
     check-sweeps-market.mjs                   second reading of the map file against the raw answers
  2. extract-v2.mjs      -> report-data.json   the model: 25 top-level keys, every number, status and sentence
     check-compare-v2.mjs                      second reading of the comparison rows against the raw answers
  3. build-report.mjs    -> competitor-analysis.html   (client cut + leak gate)
     build-report.mjs    -> action-plan.html           (service cut + other-accounts gate)
     verify-classes.mjs                        every class used in each file is styled
  4. check-documents.mjs (optional)            the two files in headless Chrome: 46 checks
StageScript (in reference/)ReadsWritesStops the run whenTime here
0ee-scan-to-seos.mjs, merge-sweep.mjsan Eagle Eyes export; the answersextra/<name>.seos.json; data/ (a copy)the export is about another place; the sweep is already held0.2 s
1sweeps-market.mjsbusiness answer, full audit, the store's place id, --tz, --wantmarket.jsona sweep header disagrees with its points; no sweep of the store0.3 s
1bcheck-sweeps-market.mjsbusiness answer, market.json, full auditlogany of its 1,697 checks disagrees0.2 s
2extract-v2.mjsthe three answers, settings, market.json, the two tablesreport-data.jsona settings, answer or rule check fails (section 6)1.4 s
2bcheck-compare-v2.mjsthe three answers, report-data.jsonlogany of its 283 checks disagrees0.2 s
3build-report.mjs (twice)report-data.json, report.css, client.js, mapview.js, fonts/the two documentsa leak, hold, other-accounts, orphan or find-box gate fails (section 9)0.2 s
3bverify-classes.mjs (twice)each documentloga class has no style0.2 s
4conformance/check-documents.mjsmodel and both documentsscreenshotsany of 46 browser checks fails14 s

run-report.mjs runs the stages in that order as child processes. The first stage that exits non-zero stops the run: no later stage runs, but what the earlier stages wrote stays in <out>, both documents included when a check after the builds failed. A finished run is exit 0 and <out>/SHA256SUMS, which is written last. Each stage's full output is kept in <out>/logs/. <out>/run-log.txt records the sha256 of the settings file and of each Eagle Eyes export, the time zone used and every stage's exit code and time; the SEOS answers' sizes and sha256 are recorded in market.json (source.inputs) and report-data.json (meta.sources). A whole run takes about 3 s without the browser check and about 17 s with it, on this machine (Windows 11, Node 24.15.0).

Requirements: Node 24 (only node: built-in modules; no npm packages). Chrome only for stage 4, which --no-browser skips. The scripts make no network calls; stage 4 talks to Chrome's DevTools port on 127.0.0.1. The documents load nothing from the network: fonts, styles and scripts are inlined (0 external resources in either file; the only outside references are ordinary links, 2 in the Competitor Analysis and 28 in the Action Plan).

3. Inputs (full detail: contract/INPUTS.md)

AnswerAPI pathFile name the runner expects
The business and every table linked to itGET /api/data/v1/businesses/{id}business-<id>.json
What the Full audit fetched (the readings)GET /api/data/v1/businesses/{id}/full-audit-resultfull-audit-<id>.json
What the Website audit fetchedGET /api/data/v1/businesses/{id}/website-audit-resultwebsite-audit-<id>.json
Every sweep in SEOS (optional)GET /api/data/v1/tables/engine_sweepsengine_sweeps-all.json
Every location in SEOS (optional)GET /api/data/v1/tables/locationslocations-all.json
  • The answers are read as SEOS returns them. The chain reads 17 tables, 19 reading kinds, 130 columns and 124 paths inside readings; INPUTS.md lists each one with the script that reads it, the model key it feeds and what happens when it is missing.
  • A reading is picked by its kind and the place_id it is about, newest fetched_at first. The store's readings use its place id, a rival's use the rival's.
  • The store is the business answer's first locations row (one store per report today; see OPEN-ITEMS G16).
  • Must be present, or no documents are built: the first businesses and locations rows; a time zone (the state table or settings.timezone); the audit run and its subject; both audit answers for the same business and run; the store's business_info reading; each sweep's engine_sweep_businesses rows; the store's bl_exhaustive reading; for the map file, at least one sweep of the store and the store's coordinates. Some of these stop with a clear message, others crash today (OPEN-ITEMS section 4).
  • Everything else may be missing. The report then says "Not measured", "could not be read" or "not in the record", or leaves the line out.
  • The fixture's input/ also holds two files SEOS is not asked for: business_info-history-green-haven.json and engine_sweep_businesses-green-haven-anywhere.json. Only the independent facts oracle reads them.

4. Settings (full detail: contract/SETTINGS.md, contract/business-settings.schema.json)

The SEOS record does not carry everything the report needs. The rest is one JSON file per business, read by extract-v2.mjs --settings (run-report.mjs always passes it). Green Haven's is fixtures/green-haven-48/settings.json:

{
  "business_id": 48,
  "brand": "Green Haven Industries",
  "short": "Green Haven",
  "brand_terms": ["green haven", "greenhaven", "green haven industries"],
  "agency": "Dispenza",
  "vertical": "Cannabis",
  "expected_searches": ["weed near me"],
  "other_market_sources": "michigan|new-?buffalo|berrien|harbor-?country|us-?12",
  "other_market_label": "Michigan"
}
KeyWhat it does
business_id (required)Guard: must equal the business answer's id.
brand, shortThe full and the short name used in sentences, tiles and comparisons.
brand_termsThe name's spellings: brand searches, linking sites that name the store, Google results tied to the store.
agencyOur tag in utm links: evidence with it is ours (team only); also "Prepared by ..." in the header.
verticalUsed when businesses.vertical is empty. Only "Cannabis" is known to the category check today.
expected_searchesMap searches the owner expects. One with no sweep on file becomes a team task and a hold; the client copy never mentions it.
other_market_sources, other_market_labelDirectory sources from another market: left out of every directory count, flagged to the team.
timezoneIANA zone, when the store's state is not in the state table.

The file fails closed: an unknown key, a file for another business, a malformed list, pattern or zone, or sources without a label each stop the build with a message. SETTINGS.md records every refusal as run, the values still accepted that should not be (OPEN-ITEMS section 5), what each key changed for Green Haven when removed, and where SEOS could store each key so the file can be written from SEOS's own record.

5. The model: report-data.json (full detail: contract/MODEL.md, contract/report-data.schema.json)

extract-v2.mjs writes the model; build-report.mjs builds both documents from the model alone (plus its own stylesheet, scripts and fonts). The model is the seam between "read SEOS" and "write the documents".

25 top-level keys: meta, business, stores, you, rivals, maps, reviews, search, website, links, listings, ai, checks, tasks, task_groups, plan, holds, ledger, compare, gaps, map, market, verdict, counts, changes. Green Haven: 43 checks, 34 tasks, 9 holds, 10 plan items, 24 comparison rows, 15 gap lines.

  • MODEL.md describes all 1,472 keys: type, Green Haven value, meaning and source, and where each one shows. The last was measured, not written: each of 1,070 keys was changed in a copy and both documents rebuilt. 225 keys reach the Competitor Analysis, 338 the Action Plan, 697 neither, and a change to 28 stops a build.
  • Closed sets checked against the code: check status (pass, watch, fail, na), weight (outcome, rank, practice, protect, data), door (maps, search, ai, website, links, overview); task owner (us, client, account, software); task group (first, ours, map, rank, reviews, page, content, links, speed, account, seos, data); and 20 more in MODEL.md.
  • node contract/validate-model.mjs contract/report-data.schema.json <report-data.json> [--plant] checks a model against the schema (no dependencies). The schema was inferred from the Green Haven model, widened from the code, and passed on 21 more models built from altered copies of the same answers.

6. The rules (full detail: contract/RULES.md, contract/rules.json, contract/check-rules.mjs)

Every threshold, status, order and cut, read off the code. rules.json holds them as data (50 check rules, 33 task rules, 11 kinds of hold, 22 comparison rows, 14 gap lines); check-rules.mjs re-evaluates them against a model and both documents and holds no threshold of its own.

  • Loss first (meta.order = 'loss-first'). The headline names the biggest loss, then the best win ("Nowhere for "weed near me"." then "First for "dispensary near me", by 1 point."). Map searches, gap lines and checks inside each tab run loss first; the board runs Wrong, To look at, Right; the plan follows a fixed order (SALES_ORDER) in buckets.
  • Statuses: pass ("Good"), watch ("Needs a look"), fail ("Needs fixing"), na ("Not measured", also a check on hold). Weight data marks a check about the run or the record, not the store: team only.
  • Holds: a number that rests on a flawed reading is shown to the team with the reason and who clears it, and never quoted to a client. 11 kinds, from a map check taken out of hours to a count stopped at a collection limit.
  • The ten client-report rules (top of extract-v2.mjs): holds; our own tags are ours; the client copy is a separate file; no capped counts; an empty read is "could not be read"; map counts printed as "58 of 121 points"; whole-website figures labelled; linking sites classified before counting; say what the tool saw; loss first. RULES.md section 7 maps each rule to the code and the gate that enforces it.
  • Gates inside the extractor: a result claimed for an expected search with no sweep on file stops the build; a line a client can see that carries our tag stops it; the headline must lead with the biggest loss; with --facts, every number the model shares with the independent facts file must agree (Green Haven: 185 shared numbers, 0 disagree).

7. The outline (full detail: contract/OUTLINE.md, contract/outline.json, contract/check-outline.mjs)

DocumentTabsBlocks (headings)
Competitor AnalysisOverview, Google Maps, Google search, Website, Links and listings, The plan91
Action PlanOverview, Google Maps, Google search, AI answers, Website, Links and listings, Tasks188

Each block in outline.json has its heading template (with {model key} slots), the model keys it reads, when it is shown, whether it is a comparison block (shown while the Compare switch is on), whether it is team-only, which document prints it, the rule that places it and the source line. check-outline.mjs reads both documents independently and checks every heading, its order and its template.

8. The wording (full detail: contract/WORDING.md, contract/wording.json, contract/check-wording.mjs)

247 entries in 16 sections: the headline rule, the frame, tiles, the map view, gaps, checks, tasks and plan, each tab, comparison cards, empty states and formats. Each entry is a fixed phrase or a template with {slots}, what each slot reads from the model, the condition that selects it, and the code line that writes it. Example, entry verdict.loss-line.none (extract-v2.mjs:1209), the line under the headline when the store is in no top 3 and not in the first 20 at any point:

For "{kw}" {short} is not in Google's top 3 at any of the {n} map points, and not in the first 20 at any of them;
{leader}, at number 1, holds {floor|if:at least }{leader_points}.

Green Haven: "For "weed near me" Green Haven is not in Google's top 3 at any of the 121 map points, and not in the first 20 at any of them; Joyleaf, at number 1, holds at least 117." Its siblings verdict.loss-line.lower (listed lower down) and verdict.loss-line.placed (in some top 3s) are chosen by the same rule from the same search's counts.

212 entries are verified: rendered from Green Haven's values, read back from the model by path, and found verbatim in a document. 35 are branches the Green Haven data does not reach, read from the code; check-wording.mjs checks that no document text fits them. Numbers, ordinals, place words, lists, plurals and escaping follow the formats table at the top of WORDING.md (en-US thousands separators; long dashes print as hyphens).

9. The two cuts (full detail: contract/RULES.md section 6)

build-report.mjs first builds one page holding both views, then cuts one view out of the file itself.

  • Competitor Analysis (--audience=client): every Service-only and team block is removed. Then the leak gate reads the finished file: no Service block, no team block, no view switch, no "software team" or "on hold", no number on hold (each hold carries its own patterns), no tool name, no utm_ tag of ours, no capped count. One hit stops the build.
  • Action Plan (--audience=service): every check, task and hold about our other accounts is left out (matched by the XACCT pattern; Green Haven: 2 checks, 1 task, 1 hold), and the build prints what it left out. Gates: no kept item may point at one left out, and the tiles may not count one. Then every Sales-only block is removed, and the finished file is read again for Sales blocks, the view switch and XACCT.
  • --doc="<name>" names the document in the browser title ("Green Haven Elizabeth · Action Plan"), the header and the overview's first line.
  • Publishing the Action Plan to a public host: reference/static-password-gate/gate.mjs encrypts the finished file (PBKDF2-SHA256, 250,000 rounds, then AES-256-GCM, decrypted in the browser). The password comes from the PASSOFF_PW environment variable and is never stored in a file. A gated file on a public host can be attacked offline, so use a long random passphrase, not a number (OPEN-ITEMS N8); better, SEOS serves the Action Plan behind its own login.

10. Determinism: what makes it repeatable, and the proof

Source of variationHow it is handled
The clockOne read: meta.built_at in the model. No document prints it, and conformance leaves it out.
The Eagle Eyes export's file timeee-scan-to-seos.mjs:70 stamps the sweep's read_at with it, and that reaches market.json and the model (never the documents). conformance.mjs pins the recorded time before the run. A fix is open (OPEN-ITEMS M13).
The input files' bytesmarket.json and the model record each input file's size and sha256. The same values written with other bytes give the same documents and different provenance fields only. A port must hash each input file's raw bytes as read. With an Eagle Eyes export folded in, the business answer recorded is merge-sweep.mjs's copy; <out>/data/merged-from.json holds the original's sha256.
The package's own bytesThe documents inline reference/report.css, client.js, mapview.js and the fonts, and conformance compares bytes, so a line-ending conversion breaks it (shown: those three files in CRLF fail conformance). Keep every file exactly as shipped; the package's .gitattributes (* -text) stops git from converting them.
Sort orderJavaScript's Array.prototype.sort is stable (ECMAScript 2019 and later), and the code sorts on explicit keys. About 15 tie-breaks call localeCompare with no locale, so they follow the host's default collation; POSIX and Danish collation were simulated and gave the same bytes here. A port must sort stably on the same keys, comparing strings with an explicit locale (en-US) or by code point.
Dates, times and number formatsIntl with the business's IANA zone and en-US formats, from Node's bundled ICU and time zone data. Pin the Node major version (24) where SEOS runs it, and run conformance after any Node upgrade.
Fonts, styles, scriptsInlined from reference/fonts, report.css, client.js and mapview.js at build time: the documents depend on those exact files.
The networkNone. Every stage reads files and writes files.

The proof, all on 2026-10-12:

  • From the raw SEOS answers (unscrubbed, outside this package), run-report.mjs rebuilt market.json and both documents byte-identical to the live Green Haven files, and report-data.json equal apart from meta.built_at.
  • From the scrubbed fixture in this package, both documents are byte-identical to the live ones: Competitor Analysis sha256 fd7a98cc…09cf92, Action Plan 3e599768…8992e7. market.json and the model differ from the live ones only in the recorded size and sha256 of the scrubbed input files (5 and 13 paths); no computed value differs.
  • node conformance/conformance.mjs: PASS (market.json and both documents byte for byte, the model apart from meta.built_at), 18.0 s, run after the last change to the fixture. The fixture's builder ran it twice earlier, and the independent check twice more: PASS every time.
  • Run twice by hand (README step 2, twice, by the independent check): every output file byte-identical apart from report-data.json's meta.built_at. With the export's file time changed: both documents byte-identical; market.json differs at 3 paths and the model at 5, as OPEN-ITEMS M13 says.

11. Variable data (full detail: VARIANTS.md)

VariantWhat changedOutcome

VARIANTS.md gives, for each variant, the checks, tasks, holds and plan items added and removed, and the sentences that appeared and went, quoted from the documents. node fixtures/green-haven-48/variants/run-variants.mjs rebuilds it, byte for byte.

12. How to build it into SEOS

Recommended route: run the reference as it is, as one step of SEOS, and accept it by conformance. Port it later only if you want it in SEOS's own language, one stage at a time, with the model as the seam. Running it as-is keeps every rule, sentence and gate that is already proven, adds no dependency beyond Node 24, and the fixture test shows at once whether the server's runtime gives the same bytes.

  1. On the SEOS host: Node 24, and this package's run-report.mjs, reference/, conformance/ and fixtures/, every file exactly as shipped (section 10). Run node conformance/conformance.mjs --no-browser; it must print CONFORMANCE: PASS. With Chrome installed, run it without --no-browser too (46 browser checks; set CHROME_PATH if Chrome is not in a usual place; run it as a normal user: as root Chrome needs --no-sandbox, which check-documents.mjs does not pass).
  2. Store each business's settings (SETTINGS.md, "Where SEOS could store it") and write them out as the settings file.
  3. Per report: save the three answers (and the two tables) for business {id} into a new folder under the names in section 3, exactly as the API returns them. The tables come in pages: merge every page into one list and keep the total. locations-all.json is every account's locations; the report reads it only to spot our own accounts on the map. Then run node run-report.mjs --data=<folder> --settings=<file> --out=<new folder> --no-browser.
  4. Exit 0 (and <out>/SHA256SUMS present): publish <out>/competitor-analysis.html to the client side and <out>/action-plan.html to the team only. Keep the rest of <out> (the map file, the model, SHA256SUMS, run-log.txt, logs/, and with an export data/ and extra/, with the browser check screenshots/) as the record of what was read and built. Any other exit: publish nothing, even when documents are in <out>: a stage after the builds (the class check, the browser check) may have failed with both documents already written (OPEN-ITEMS E13). run-log.txt and logs/ name the stage that stopped the run and why. That is by design: a report that cannot be built correctly is not published.

What SEOS has to add for this to work for any business, beyond the code (OPEN-ITEMS section 1): stored settings; a sweep of every expected search (until then an Eagle Eyes export can be folded in with --extra-sweep); and three data defects the report itself flags in Green Haven's answers (another account's readings in the full audit, another market's directory sources, map checks searched from a far vantage).

Before reports go out for businesses other than Green Haven, the reference code needs the fixes in OPEN-ITEMS sections 2 and 4: today a few sentences carry Green Haven's facts (for example "for Elizabeth and the towns around it"), and some missing readings crash a stage.

Porting later. Port stage 2 (answers to model) or stage 3 (model to documents) on its own, and accept each with the same fixture:

  • A model from a port: node conformance/conformance.mjs --model=<its report-data.json> (equal to expected/ apart from meta.built_at and meta.facts_check, the record of the Green Haven facts check, which a port need not have; every differing path is printed), then validate-model.mjs, check-rules.mjs and check-wording.mjs. Build the port's fixture model from fixtures/green-haven-48/input/ with the export's file time pinned to the one in fixture.json (OPEN-ITEMS M13), as conformance.mjs does.
  • Documents from a port: node conformance/conformance.mjs --documents=<folder holding both files> (byte for byte; the first differing byte is shown with its context), then check-outline.mjs and check-wording.mjs.
  • A port must also hash input files' raw bytes, sort stably on the same keys, and format numbers, dates and escapes as the formats table in WORDING.md says.

0. Decisions for James

  1. Who fixes the reference code, and when. Recommended: we fix sections 2, 4 and 5 (and section 6, the 8 defects that show in today's Green Haven documents) in our reference code, rebuild Green Haven, and re-issue this package as version 2, before SEOS builds this report for any other business. Reason: the contract files, the fixture's expected outputs and the conformance test are all generated from the reference, so fixing it there keeps one source of truth. Section 6 changes Green Haven's two live documents slightly (the preview site would be republished). Dan can start on section 1 and on wiring the runner in the meantime; nothing there waits on these fixes.
  2. The Compare switch in the Action Plan (N1). It opens "on" today; the code's own comment says "off" in the Service view. Which is meant? Changing it changes behaviour on open, not the file's text.
  3. Businesses outside cannabis. If SEOS will run this report for other trades, section 3 is needed (one "vertical profile" per trade). If not yet, only V1 is needed now (it misfires for any vertical the code does not know).

1. SEOS side (for Dan)

  • S1. Another account's readings in a business's answer. GET /businesses/48/full-audit-result carries 4 Google Analytics and Search Console readings of 2 other accounts' websites, plus 24 readings bought for other reports (Oct 5 and Oct 6, 2026), all 24 about businesses hundreds of miles away. The report uses none of them and flags them to the team (check answer-scope, task answer-isolation, both team-only and left out of the Action Plan). Fix in SEOS: a business's answers hold only that business's readings. In the fixture those 4 rows keep their kind, place, website and time, with the request and result emptied (input/SCRUBBED.md). Found by A, C2; seen in expected/report-data.json.
  • S2. Another market's directory sources. Green Haven's directory list holds 10 sources that name Michigan places, left over from another store's list; all 10 came back "could not be read". The report leaves them out of every count (136 checked, not 146) and flags them (check directory-sources). Fix in SEOS: give each source a market in the source registry and build each store's list from its own market. Then the other_market_sources setting is not needed. Found by B; seen in expected/report-data.json.
  • S3. Map checks searched from far away. 31 of the 298 business rows in Green Haven's 3 map checks sit 1,078 to 1,310 miles away, near where the scan engine searches from (Council Bluffs, Iowa). For "weed near me" they are in a first 20 at 120 of 121 points, and one reached a top 3 at 66 points. The report reads each list again without them and quotes only counts that do not change (check scan-market). Fix in SEOS: search from the store's market, or return the vantage with each sweep so the report can name it from the data (see G2). Seen in expected/report-data.json.
  • S4. Sweeps of the expected searches. SEOS holds no "weed near me" sweep of Green Haven; the fixture folds in the owner's Eagle Eyes scan 320 (--extra-sweep). For SEOS to build this report alone, it must sweep each expected search (same grid as its other sweeps, in opening hours), for example from scan_schedules.keywords. Without one, the report shows that search as "not measured" with a team task, and the client copy never mentions it (VARIANTS.md, no-weed-scan). Shown.
  • S5. Where the settings live. Each settings key, and the column SEOS could hold it in, is in contract/SETTINGS.md ("Where SEOS could store it"). Two notes: businesses.vertical is null for Green Haven (fill it), and whether locations.citation_vendor_tag is the same tag as agency was not verified.
  • S6. Whole lists from the table answers. engine_sweeps-all.json and locations-all.json must hold every row. The extractor counts rows, not the answer's total (M12), and paging past 1,000 rows was not tried.

  • K6. sweeps-market.mjs:23: --tz is not checked (a bad zone crashed it) and defaults to America/New_York. run-report.mjs checks the zone and passes the same one to both scripts. Fix: check it as extract-v2.mjs:81 does. Shown. Found by A, B.

6. Defects in today's Green Haven documents

Fixing these changes both live documents (or the Action Plan), so expected/ is rewritten and the preview republished: decision 1.

  • W1. build-report.mjs:565: the pattern /, d+:d+ [AP]M$/ lacks its backslashes, so the "What was read, and when" row prints every map check's full time ("Sun, Oct 11, 7:21 PM, Sun, Oct 11, 7:26 PM, Mon, Oct 12, 10:31 AM") instead of the days. Fix: /, \d+:\d+ [AP]M$/, as on line 229. Seen (both). Found by A, C1, C2.
  • W2. build-report.mjs:387 with extract-v2.mjs:23-24: the Action Plan says "A far-away business in a point's top 3 would put that check on hold"; the code holds a check only when the far businesses change the store's own count. "weed near me" has one in a top 3 at 66 points and is rightly not held. Fix: the note and the comment, not the rule. Seen (Action Plan). Found by C2.
  • W3. "Check both searches again": see G3. Seen (Action Plan).
  • W4. build-report.mjs:313, 315-316: "it is in the top 3 at none at 0 of 121 points"; factor names lower-cased whole ("gbp points at homepage"). Fix: a comma as on line 390; lower-case only the first letter. Seen (Action Plan). Found by C1.
  • W5. build-report.mjs:538: the Service table of directory verdicts prints codes ("not-listed", "nap-incomplete"). Fix: words, as extract-v2.mjs:644 does. Seen (Action Plan). Found by C1.
  • W6. build-report.mjs:213, 399: "5 stars" on the listing row and Reviews card, "5.0 stars" everywhere else. Fix: one decimal. Seen (both). Found by C1.
  • W7. extract-v2.mjs:532 (printed at build-report.mjs:523 in the Action Plan, and through check link-wave, extract-v2.mjs:869, in both documents): shared-title waves print stored dates ("first seen 2026-09-11 to 2026-10-12"); every other date reads "Oct 11, 2026". Seen (both). Found by C1.
  • W8. build-report.mjs:36: the Action Plan leaves the other-account task out but keeps every task's number, so the numbers skip (31, then 33). Fix: renumber after the cut, or say the numbers follow the full report. Seen. Found by C1.

7. Rule edges and latent defects (no effect on Green Haven today)

  • E1. extract-v2.mjs:1210: the placed loss line drops "at least" when number 1's count is a floor. Read. C1.
  • E2. extract-v2.mjs:431, 435: the phone speed band reads the raw score but the page prints it rounded (a raw 0.895 prints "90 of 100" with "Needs a look"). Read. C2.
  • E3. extract-v2.mjs:739, 910, 1205: losses are sorted three times with different tie-breaks; on a tie the headline could name another search than the first map and the map-gap task. Fix: one comparator. Read. C2.
  • E4. extract-v2.mjs:1030-1031: the chain-rival hold names a link strength its leak patterns do not cover (not printed today). Read. C2.
  • E5. build-report.mjs:38-39: two tests of the Action Plan's orphan gate read fields the model never has, so they never fire. Read and confirmed on the model. C2.
  • E6. build-report.mjs:29-37 (gate at 676-686): the Action Plan's other-accounts cut matches a text pattern, so wording decides what is left out. Measured: with the other-account readings dropped whole, answer-scope and answer-isolation stop matching and stay in (761,380 to 764,637 bytes). Fix: the extractor marks such items with a field and the builder cuts by it, keeping the text gate as a second check. Shown. A.
  • E7. extract-v2.mjs:820: check connected says "Neither is connected" when one of the two is. Read. C2.
  • E8. extract-v2.mjs:799: review-count passes against the smallest store beside it (Green Haven's has 6 ratings). Read. C2.
  • E9. extract-v2.mjs:837: check title opens no task on watch. Read. C2.
  • E10. build-report.mjs:115: the map subtitle says "every one taken in opening hours" whenever no check is known to be outside them, including checks whose hours are unknown. Read. C2.
  • E11. mapview.js:110, 122, 125: "Number 1" in the map's trend tooltip and its every-search table is the first business in the field, far-away ones included, while the board, the picker and the extractor never make a far business number 1 (mapview.js:33, 81, 133; extract-v2.mjs:269-271). Where a far business has the most top-3 points, the table would disagree with the headline. Not Green Haven's case (Joyleaf has 117; the far business reached 66). Fix: the first business in the field that is not far. Read. Found by the independent check.
  • E12. extract-v2.mjs:917, task rescan-open-hours: gives Monday's hours as the window for every day (Green Haven posts 10 AM to 10 PM on Monday, 9 PM closing on Saturday, 11 AM opening on Sunday). The task opens only when a map check ran outside opening hours; Green Haven's three did not, so today's documents do not carry it. Fix: the week's hours. Read. Found by C2.
  • E13. run-report.mjs:87-91: a stage that fails after the builds (the class check, the browser check, or the Action Plan build after the Competitor Analysis) stops the run but leaves the documents already written in <out>. SPEC section 12 says to publish only on exit 0 with <out>/SHA256SUMS present (written last). Fix, if wanted: write the documents under a temporary name and rename them after the last stage. Shown. Found by the independent check.

8. Comments and notes that disagree with the code (no effect on output)

  • N1. build-report.mjs:12-13 says Compare starts off in the Service view; client.js:50-53 starts it on in both (decision 2).
  • N2. extract-v2.mjs:1051-1053: a "nearby" comparison set no row uses; :890-891: a pass wording for rival-rows that is never emitted.
  • N3. extract-v2.mjs:23-24: the rule 1 comment (see W2). Our working notes (DATA-NOTES.md, not in this package) still describe the old order "lead with what they built"; the code is loss-first.
  • N4. merge-sweep.mjs:33-35: the merged answer keeps the old counts header (nothing reads it).
  • N5. report-data.json ledger is built and never printed (build-report.mjs:45).
  • N6. build-report.mjs keeps branches for an older High Society file (no meta.v2): inert for this report.
  • N7. extract-v2.mjs:825, 1151, 1353 and build-report.mjs:264, 452: the AI answers tab says SEOS has no answer-engine surface yet and nothing was collected; ai is a constant { collected: false }. True today; revisit when SEOS collects AI answers. Seen (Action Plan; the tab is not in the Competitor Analysis).
  • N8. reference/static-password-gate/gate.mjs:42 asks phones for digits (inputmode="numeric"). A published gated file can be attacked offline: as an estimate, not measured, an 8-digit number falls to one current GPU in about an hour at 250,000 PBKDF2-SHA256 rounds, and each extra digit multiplies that by ten. Use a long random passphrase, or serve the Action Plan behind SEOS's own login.

9. Not verified

  • The browser checks (check-documents.mjs, conformance without --no-browser) ran only on Windows 11 with Chrome at its Windows path. The macOS and Linux paths, and running as root (--no-sandbox), were not tried.
  • Pinning the export's file time needs a file system that keeps milliseconds (NTFS here). On one that does not, conformance.mjs is written to stop with a message; that was read from the code, not run.
  • run-report.mjs with more than one --extra-sweep: written, not run (one export exists).
  • Other businesses, other trades and multi-location brands were not run, beyond the six scripted variants on Green Haven's own data. The model schema was inferred from one model and passed on 21 altered ones from the same answers.
  • 35 wording entries are branches the Green Haven data does not reach: read from the code, and checked absent from both documents, not rendered.
  • Paging of GET /api/data/v1/tables/* past 1,000 rows; whether locations.citation_vendor_tag is the agency tag; any Eagle Eyes export other than scan 320.
  • Several rules were read from the code and never met by a model that holds them (RULES.md section 8 and parts/C2-rules.json list them).
  • About 15 tie-breaks use localeCompare without a locale, so they follow the host's default collation. POSIX and Danish collation were simulated and gave the same bytes on this fixture; other data could tie differently.
  • The rebuild from the raw, unscrubbed SEOS answers (SPEC section 10) was run by the fixture's builder, not by the independent check, which could read the raw answers only through the privacy scanner.

The answers are read as saved, with no network call. The business answer holds every table linked to the business except the readings. The readings are in the two audit answers.

Checks across the answers (extract-v2 stops when one fails):

  • Each audit answer's business_id must equal businesses[0].id: "<file> is about business <x>, not <y>". Green Haven: 48, 48, 48.
  • Each audit answer's audit must be its own kind: "<file> is not the full-audit answer" (or website-audit). Green Haven: "full-audit", "website-audit".
  • The full-audit answer's tables.audit_runs[0].id must be the record's main run (the run with the most steps). Green Haven: 6d717f58bda5982e = 6d717f58bda5982e (60 steps).
  • locations[0].place_id must be the subject of that run.

How a reading is picked: by kind and by place_id together, from both audit answers, the newest fetched_at first. The store's readings use its place id. A rival's use its place id. The website audit keys each rival's front page as site:<domain>.

What must be there, or the documents are not built (from the code; the two crashes were tried on altered copies):

  • the first businesses row and the first locations row;
  • a time zone: locations.state in the state table of extract-v2.mjs, or timezone in the settings file;
  • an audit_runs row whose businesses list names a subject, and that subject's place id on the location row;
  • both audit answers, about the same business, the full audit about the same run;
  • the store's business_info reading, with its item;
  • for every sweep with points, its engine_sweep_businesses rows (without them extract-v2 crashes);
  • the store's bl_exhaustive reading (without it extract-v2 writes links: null and build-report.mjs crashes);
  • for the map file (sweeps-market.mjs): at least one sweep of the store, the store's lat and lng, and sweep headers that agree with their points.

Everything else can be missing. The report then says "not measured", "could not be read" or "not in the record", or leaves the line out, as each section below says.

GET /api/data/v1/businesses/{id}: the tables

"Present" counts the rows of the Green Haven answer in which the column holds a value (not null). "Catalog" says whether SEOS's table catalog (GET /api/data/v1/tables, saved as tables.json) lists the column. "Partly" is not a defect by itself: a value can be missing for a real reason. For example cells[].rank is empty in the row of scan 320 because the store is in no list at any of its points.

The readings: GET /api/data/v1/businesses/{id}/full-audit-result and /website-audit-result

Each audit answer is {business_id, audit, keys, kinds, counts, tables: {vendor_readings, audit_runs}, not_included}. The chain reads business_id, audit, tables.audit_runs[0] (the full audit: its id; the website audit: id, started_at, finished_at and steps, for meta.website_run) and tables.vendor_readings. Of each reading it reads kind, place_id, fetched_at, and per kind the paths below (target, request, result).

"Readings" counts by place: store, rival (the run's other businesses), field (a business in one of the store's sweeps), site (a website audit site:<domain> key) and other. "Present" counts the readings of that kind in which the path holds a value. A path with ~ means every key matching the pattern, and * means every key.

The two optional lists

--all-sweeps (GET /api/data/v1/tables/engine_sweeps): {table, columns, total, limit, offset, rows}. sweeps-market reads rows[].scan_id, subject, keyword and finished_at, and total. It lists the store's sweeps it did not read (market.source.all_sweeps), and calls an absence "not proof" when total exceeds the rows held. extract-v2 reads only the number of rows, for the sentence "None of the <n> sweeps in the software is a <phrase> check of this store". Green Haven: 166 rows, total 166, 2 of this store. Without it the sentence is left out, and sweeps-market's market.source.all_sweeps is null. The API pages at limit. Save every page.

--locations (GET /api/data/v1/tables/locations): extract-v2 reads rows[].place_id, business_id, name, city and state. A location of another business whose place id is in the store's sweeps is one of our own accounts on this map. It feeds the own-accounts check and a hold (team only), both of which build-report.mjs leaves out of the Action Plan. They are never in the Competitor Analysis. Green Haven: 54 rows; 3 belong to other businesses and sit in this store's sweeps. Without it there is no own-accounts check or hold.

A sweep from Eagle Eyes (ee-scan-to-seos.mjs)

When SEOS holds no sweep of a search the owner expects, an Eagle Eyes scan export can stand in. node ee-scan-to-seos.mjs <export.json> <store place id> <out.json> turns it into SEOS's own sweep rows (engine_sweeps, engine_sweep_cells, engine_sweep_businesses, engine_sweep_fields, engine_actors). merge-sweep.mjs then appends them to a copy of the business answer. It refuses a sweep id already held and a sweep about another store.

The export shape it reads:

  • Top level: id, status, error, created_at, finished_at, request, results, metrics.
  • request: place_id, business_name, keyword, grid_size, radius, unit, center_lat, center_lng, excluded_points, feed_depth, zoom, vantage.label.
  • results[], one per point: index, row, col, lat, lng, rank, error, listings.
  • results[].listings[], best first: position, place_id, name, address, category, rating, reviews, lat, lng.
  • metrics: found_points, top3_points, solv, atrp, arp, total_points, listings_seen.

It stops (EE CONVERT FAILED) when:

  • there is no request or no results;
  • request.place_id is not the store;
  • any point has an error;
  • status is "failed" for any reason other than "no point named this business" (a scan where the store is found nowhere is kept as a real result);
  • a listing's position is not its place in the list;
  • a point's rank is not the store's place in that point's list;
  • a metrics value disagrees with what the points give.

excluded_points are left out and named in exclusion_note. feed_depth "centre_whole" becomes started_how "whole_feed". read_at is the export file's modification time.

Green Haven (scan 320, eagleeyes-scan-320-weed-near-me.json): about the store: yes; 121 points, 0 errored, 2423 listings. Fields present: top level 8 of 8, request 12 of 12, point fields 8 of 8 on every point, listing fields 7 of 9 on every listing (rating 2183/2423, reviews 0/2423), metrics 6 of 7.

How to run

D=_data/green-haven-2026-10-12-with-ee320
node <this folder>/inputs-census.mjs $D/business-48.json $D/full-audit-48.json $D/website-audit-48.json \
  --all-sweeps=$D/engine_sweeps-all.json --locations=$D/locations-all.json --tables=$D/tables.json --openapi=$D/openapi.json \
  --ee=_data/green-haven-2026-10-12/extra-ee/eagleeyes-scan-320-weed-near-me.json --md=<this folder>/INPUTS.md

The census prints counts and names only. It never prints a value from a reading, and never anything from the readings about other accounts beyond how many there are.

Per-business settings

The settings file, key by key

contract/SETTINGS.md 13 KB

Per-business settings

The SEOS record does not carry everything the report needs about a business. The rest comes from one small JSON file per business, read by extract-v2.mjs --settings=<file>. The file for Green Haven is green-haven/business-settings-48.json. The exact rules are in business-settings.schema.json next to this file.

How the file is read (settingsFrom, extract-v2.mjs lines 72-83):

  • A key the extractor does not know stops the build.
  • business_id is required and must equal businesses[0].id of the business answer.
  • A file for another business stops the build.
  • A malformed list, pattern or time zone stops the build.
  • other_market_sources without other_market_label stops the build.
  • Every stop prints EXTRACT FAILED: <message> and exits with code 1. One exception: a file holding only null crashes with a TypeError (also exit code 1).
  • Without --settings the extractor uses its built-in SETTINGS table, which knows only businesses 26 and 48. Any other business then gets no settings at all, and nothing warns about it.

The table

"Effect" names the report keys and the parts of the documents each setting changes. The Green Haven column comes from green-haven/business-settings-48.json. "In the record today" was checked against _data/green-haven-2026-10-12-with-ee320/business-48.json (the business answer) and tables.json (SEOS's table catalog).

Findings (also in parts/B-contract.json)

  • extract-v2.mjs:78 accepts an empty brand_terms list. Lines 568 and 610 then build a pattern that matches everything. Fix: refuse an empty list in settingsFrom.
  • extract-v2.mjs:79-80 never checks the type of other_market_sources. Any value is turned into text and compiled, so "" or {} silently drops the directories. Fix: require a string with a non-blank character.
  • extract-v2.mjs:768 compares expected_searches with the lower-cased sweep keywords exactly. Fix: trim and lower-case each phrase in settingsFrom.
  • extract-v2.mjs:791 adds the fix-category task when the vertical is not in CATEGORY, while the check itself says "not measured". Fix: no task unless CATEGORY[business.vertical] exists.
  • extract-v2.mjs:76 prints "for business 48, not 48" for a quoted id. Fix: print the value's type, or accept a numeric string.
  • extract-v2.mjs:75 crashes with a TypeError when the file is null. Fix: refuse anything that is not a plain object first.
  • extract-v2.mjs:84 falls back to the hard-coded SETTINGS table and gives an unknown business {} with no warning. Fix: make --settings required, or stop when the business is in neither.

The report model

Every key of report-data.json and where it shows

contract/MODEL.md 266 KB

The report model (report-data.json)

Generated by make-model-schema.mjs with report-data.schema.json. Edit the script, not this file.

extract-v2.mjs writes this model from the SEOS answers, and build-report.mjs builds both documents from it alone. Nobody writes anything at build time. This file lists every key of the model, grouped by its 25 top-level keys. The Green Haven model (SEOS business 48, green-haven/report-data.json) is the example throughout.

How each column was made:

  • Type is inferred from the Green Haven model: every number is "number", and null is listed where it occurs. Then an overlay in the script, checked against the code, sets what one model cannot show: the type of a key that is null or empty here, values the code fixes ("always ..."), closed sets ("one of ..."), keys the code can add or leave out, and nulls the code can write.
  • Green Haven is the value in that model for a key outside any list. Inside a list it reads "(per item)".
  • Meaning and source was written from the code of extract-v2.mjs and sweeps-market.mjs: what the key is, and which inputs and rule make it. The input names are those of INPUTS.md.
  • Competitor Analysis and Action Plan are measured, not written. For every key that holds a value, the script changed that one key in a copy of the model and built both documents from the copy (build-report.mjs ... --audience=client --doc="Competitor Analysis" and --audience=service --doc="Action Plan"). It then named the first changed place in each tab ("tab > the heading above it"), or the embedded data that changed ("the find box", "the map data"). Text gets a marker and its last digit moves, a number moves, and true/false flips. A key in a list is changed in every item at once.
    • "No change seen" means neither file changed. The key can still be read by a test whose answer did not flip.
    • "The build stops" means the documents depend on the key: the changed value broke a rule or a lookup.
    • For an object or a list, the column joins what its keys showed.

Totals (Green Haven)

  • 1,472 keys described: every key, list item shape and map value once. The tables also list 67 rows for map.town and map.won[], which copy the shape of map.searches[] and are empty here.
  • 1,070 keys hold a value and were probed. 31 could not be probed: they are null in this model and the code gives them no simple type.
  • 225 change the Competitor Analysis and 338 change the Action Plan when they change. 13 change only the Competitor Analysis, and 120 only the Action Plan.
  • 697 changed neither document when they changed ("no change seen").
  • 28 make one of the builds stop when they change.

Validating a model

node validate-model.mjs report-data.schema.json <report-data.json> [--plant]

validate-model.mjs has no dependencies. It applies the part of JSON Schema these schemas use, and refuses a schema that uses anything else. --plant also checks three mistakes planted in a copy of the data: a missing required key, a wrong enum value and a wrong type. The results are in parts/B-contract.json.

What the schema can and cannot say:

  • It was inferred from one model and widened from the code. It was then tried on 21 more models built in a scratch folder from the same SEOS answers: 15 with one setting left out or changed, 4 with one input left out, and 2 from the original folder without scan 320 (with and without a market file). All pass; the commands are in parts/B-contract.json. A key that is required here but that another business's reading lacks (extract-v2.mjs then writes no key) fails validation. That usually means a gap in the data worth a look, not a fault in the schema.
  • Counts are "number", not "integer": one model cannot tell a count from a rating that happens to be whole (business.rating is 5 here).
  • The High Society shape (meta.v2 absent) is not covered. meta.v2 must be true. build-report.mjs keeps branches for that older shape; they are inert when meta.v2 is true.

links

market

The market file (sweeps-market.mjs output, the HS market.json shape) embedded whole; null without --market. build-report.mjs and mapview.js draw the map from subject, alphabet, biz, geoms and scans; the rest is kept for the team and the checks.

Competitor Analysis: shows in Overview > The map, point by point; the map data (redraw); Overview > The top of the map; Overview > You; Overview (headline); Overview > Number 1. Action Plan: shows in Overview > The map, point by point; the map data (redraw); Overview > The top of the map; Overview > You; Overview > Ask the client; Overview > Number 1.

Decision rules

Every threshold, status, order and cut

contract/RULES.md 130 KB

The decision rules

Every threshold, status, order and cut that turns the SEOS numbers into the two documents: the Competitor Analysis (the Sales view, client-safe) and the Action Plan (the Service view, a team document). Read off extract-v2.mjs (it writes the model, report-data.json) and build-report.mjs (it writes the documents) as they stand on 2026-10-12. A reference like extract-v2.mjs:792 is a line of that file in Product/seos-report/.

Three files go together:

  • RULES.md (this file): the rules in words.
  • rules.json: sections 2 to 5 as data. Each status rule, value line, client-safe flag, sentence and sort is written as a small expression (the language is described in rules.json under expressions).
  • check-rules.mjs: reads a model and rules.json, evaluates every rule it can and compares the result with the model. It holds no threshold of its own: change a number in rules.json and the check changes with it.
node check-rules.mjs <report-data.json> [--rules=rules.json] [--md=RULES.md] \
     [--client-doc=<competitor-analysis.html>] [--service-doc=<action-plan.html>] [--json=<out.json>]

Scope. Green Haven Industries, Elizabeth NJ (SEOS business 48), the model extract-v2.mjs writes from SEOS's current API (meta.v2 = true, meta.order = 'loss-first'). build-report.mjs also holds branches for an older High Society file without meta.v2; they are inert when meta.v2 is true and are not described here.

Words used here.

  • The store: the business the report is about. Rivals: the three stores the SEOS run names beside it. The field: every business a map check lists. Far: more than 150 miles (241.4 km) from the store (extract-v2.mjs:206).
  • Number 1 and number 2: the businesses with the most and the second most points in Google's top 3 in a map check, far businesses left out.
  • A check: one line of the health checks, with an area (the code calls it a door), a weight, a status, a title, a value, a line of detail and the task it names.
  • Status: pass (shown "Good"), watch ("Needs a look"), fail ("Needs fixing"), na ("Not measured"; also a check on hold).
  • Weight: outcome, rank, practice, protect, or data (about the run or the record, not the store: team only).
  • Ours (internal): about our own work or tags. Team only.
  • On hold: a number that rests on a flawed reading. The team sees it with the reason; a client never does.
  • Client-safe: a comparison row a client may see (sales: true in the model).

1. Order: losing first, winning last

meta.order = 'loss-first' (extract-v2.mjs:1349) is the owner's ordering. build-report.mjs reads it (LOSS, line 54) and runs every list below with the store's losses first and its wins last. check-rules.mjs recomputes 1.1, 1.2, the plan of 1.8 and 1.9 from the model, and checks 1.4, 1.5, the client board of 1.6 and the buckets of 1.8 in the two Green Haven documents. 1.3 and 1.7 are read from the code only.

1.1 The map searches (maps.searches)

extract-v2.mjs:739-740. Every search on file, in this order:

  1. Losses before wins (you_lead false first). The store leads a search when it is in a top 3 at one point or more and has at least as many top-3 points as number 2 (a tie with number 2 counts as a lead: extract-v2.mjs:210, 272).
  2. Among losses: a search where the store is in no top 3 first; then the largest gap to number 1 as a share of the points, (number 1's points - the store's points) / points, largest first.
  3. Among wins: the narrowest margin over number 2 first, (the store's points - number 2's points) / points, so the widest win is last.

Green Haven: "weed near me" (0 of 121 points, in no first 20), then "cannabis near me" (37 of 111; number 1 holds 88), then "dispensary near me" (58 of 121, number 1 by one point over 57).

Where this order shows: the map on the overview opens on the first search that is not on hold and not won (build-report.mjs:109); the client overview's map tiles are the first three searches not on hold, the first one the lead tile (build-report.mjs:186-192); the Google Maps tab heading runs the searches in this order (build-report.mjs:390). The table "Every search checked on the map" (build-report.mjs:241-247) is built only when there is no market file, so not for Green Haven.

1.2 The headline (verdict): which search heads the page

extract-v2.mjs:1201-1218. Only searches not on hold count. Losses run as in 1.1, with one more tie-break: number 1's share of the points, highest first (extract-v2.mjs:1205). Wins run the other way from 1.1: the widest margin first (extract-v2.mjs:1206), so the headline names the widest win.

  • a (the big line) = the first loss's head, or the first win's head when there is no loss.
  • b (the second line) = the first win's head when there are losses and wins; else the second loss's head; else empty.
  • A loss head: "Nowhere for "<search>"." (no top-3 point and in no first 20), "Outside the top 3 for "<search>"." (no top-3 point), else "<First, Second ... Twelfth, or Number k> for "<search>"." by the store's place among the businesses.
  • A win head: "First for "<search>"" or "Tied first ..." (level with number 2), plus ", by k point(s)" when the margin is 1 or 2.
  • The lead paragraph runs every loss line, then every win line, then "It has <ratings> Google ratings at <stars> stars."
  • With no search off hold: a = "<ratings> ratings at <stars> stars.", b = "The map check comes next."
  • Gate: the extractor stops when a loss exists and line a does not name the first loss (extract-v2.mjs:1252, "EXTRACT FAILED: the headline does not lead with the biggest loss").

Green Haven: a = Nowhere for "weed near me"., b = First for "dispensary near me", by 1 point.

1.3 The first loss (L1)

extract-v2.mjs:910-912. The first search not on hold and not won, sorted as the losses in 1.1 (no further tie-break). L1 names the map-gap task (its title, client title, benefit and done-when) and the "-1" gap lines (ratings-1, stars-1 ...), which set the store's Google listing beside L1's number 1. Green Haven: L1 is "weed near me".

1.4 The gap lines ("The gap to number 1")

build-report.mjs:134 (gapOrder). Lines where the store is behind first, lines where it is level or ahead last; inside each part, whole-website lines after the others; then the largest deficit first (deficit: section 5). The Competitor Analysis leaves out lines on hold.

Green Haven, Competitor Analysis: map-seos-320, replies-90, ratings-1, photos-1, map-seos-353, speed, then the whole-website visits, searches, strength, then level or ahead: ways-1, map-seos-352, stars-1, details-1, clean-sites. The Action Plan adds phone-named (on hold) after map-seos-353.

1.5 The checks inside each tab

build-report.mjs:55-56, 160-165, 175-178. fail, then watch, then not measured, then pass; checks with the same status keep the extractor's order. The Competitor Analysis lists the store's checks a client sees (section 2). The Action Plan lists the store's checks, then a separate block "Checks on the data itself" (weight data), sorted the same way.

Green Haven, Google Maps tab, Competitor Analysis: map-seos-353 and map-seos-320 (fail), review-pace, replies, review-velocity (watch), then nine passes.

1.6 The Wrong / To look at / Right board

build-report.mjs:146-151. Three columns in this order: Wrong (fail), To look at (watch), Right (pass). Checks not measured are named in a note below. The client board leaves out overview, data, internal and AI checks; the team board leaves out overview checks. Inside a column the extractor's order holds. On hold, the client reads "Check to come" in place of the value (build-report.mjs:147).

Green Haven: the Competitor Analysis board holds 2 wrong, 14 to look at, 15 right; the Action Plan board 7, 16 and 17.

1.7 The comparison cards

build-report.mjs:98-100. In each grid of cards, the card where the store is furthest behind comes first (the most entries above the store), cards where it leads or is level come last, and anything that is not a comparison row sits between; ties keep their order. On the Google Maps tab the map-check cards are first sorted worst place first (no place counts as 99) and first place last, then by the same standing (build-report.mjs:389). Not recomputed by check-rules.mjs.

Green Haven, Google Maps tab: map-320 (5th), map-353 (3rd), map-352 (1st); then ratings, photos, stars.

1.8 The plan (SALES_ORDER) and its buckets (BOARD)

extract-v2.mjs:1006-1010. The Competitor Analysis plan follows one fixed list, the owner's order of the kinds of work, losing first:

rescan-open-hours, map-gap, reply-reviews, review-gap, store-page-check, speed, claim-listing, fix-category, add-service-options, fix-hours, reply-low-stars, low-star-subjects, content-gap, listings-hand-check, link-list, junk-links, connect-google.

A task takes its place in the plan when it was opened, is not internal, is not service_only and belongs to us or the client. The plan prints its client title (else its title), its benefit, and "With your team" for a client task. Gate: a client-facing task missing from SALES_ORDER stops the extractor ("tasks with no place in the sales plan", line 1010).

The "What is missing" cards (build-report.mjs:202-207) group the plan in buckets, in this order: The map, Reviews, The store page, Speed, Pages and content, Listings and links, Google Analytics and Search Console; a plan item in no bucket goes last under "The Google listing" (claim-listing, fix-category, add-service-options, fix-hours). The plan tab's lead line names the buckets in the order the plan first meets them (build-report.mjs:550).

Green Haven plan (10): 1 "Win "weed near me" on the map", 2 "Answer every new review", 3 "Keep new reviews coming as fast as your rivals" (with your team), 4 "Make sure Google reads the store page", 5 "Speed up the store page on a phone", 6 "Name the searches your rivals win and you miss", 7 "Check the listings that matter", 8 "Get links from the sites that link to your rivals", 9 "Watch the wave of link-selling pages", 10 "Connect Google Analytics and Search Console" (with your team). Buckets: The map 1, Reviews 2, The store page 1, Speed 1, Pages and content 1, Listings and links 3, Google Analytics and Search Console 1.

1.9 The Action Plan's task list

extract-v2.mjs:969-1000. Tasks are numbered by group (the order of task_groups in rules.json: Before anything else, Ours to put right, The map, Listing basics, Reviews, The store page, Pages and content, Listings and links, Speed, For the account manager, Found by the software, For the software team), then the task's place in its group's list (99 when not listed), then failing tasks first, then area (Google Maps, Google search, Website, Links and listings, AI answers, Overview), then id.

Green Haven: 1 client-questions, 2 map-gap, 3 connect-google, 4 reply-reviews, 5 review-gap, 6 store-page-check, 7 content-gap, 8 listings-hand-check, 9 link-list, 10 junk-links, 11 speed, 12 to 26 the fifteen SEOS findings, 27 to 34 the software team's eight.

2. Health checks

How a check reaches each document.

  • A check names a task (check.task). The task is opened only when the check's status is not pass (extract-v2.mjs:991). A task's status is fail when any check that opened it fails, else the status of the first check that opened it, else watch (extract-v2.mjs:987-988).
  • A client sees a check when its area is Google Maps, Google search, Website or Links and listings, its weight is not data and it is not ours (build-report.mjs:148, 158, 161, 547). The AI tab is team-only. Overview checks are shown only through their task.
  • On hold, the client reads "Check to come" in place of the value, and the check's client line (sales in the model) in place of the detail when it has one (build-report.mjs:147, 157, 547).
  • The area tiles count each area's checks that are not data and not ours (extract-v2.mjs:1221-1222).
  • Thresholds are fixed numbers in the code: 0.8 of number 1's points; 0.9 of the points listed; 4.5 and 4.0 stars; 2 ways to shop; 80% replies; 0.8 of the earlier review pace; 0.8 of the rivals' lower median velocity; 7 days of hours; lab score 0.9 and 0.5; 300 words; under half the browser's words; title 30 to 65 and description 70 characters; 30% link sellers; 20% new link sellers; vendor score 10 for the link list; 5 outside sites; half the directories; 150 miles. None reads the vertical, except the main category (CATEGORY: Cannabis only).

2.2 Google Maps checks

map-{search key}

extract-v2.mjs:752-760 · Google Maps · weight outcome · title "Number 1 on the map for "{kw}""

  • Made when: one per search on file: every search in the market file (--market) plus every SEOS sweep the market file does not carry (same search, same day). The key is the market file's scan key (e.g. seos-353) or scan-<sweep id> for a sweep from the record alone.
  • Status: na when the search is on hold; pass when the store is number 1 (its top-3 point count is at least number 2's and above 0); watch when its top-3 points are at least 80% of number 1's; fail otherwise.
  • As rules.json writes it: hold -> na; you_lead -> pass; you >= leader_points * 0.8 -> watch; else fail
  • Value: "Not found" when the store has no top-3 point and is in no first 20; else "<you> of <n> points"
  • Line: Number 1: "Number 1 for "<kw>": in Google's top 3 at <you> of <n> points, <k> points ahead of / level with <number 2> (<points>). Checked <when>." Otherwise: "<Not in the first 20 at any of the <n> points | In the first 20 at <found> of <n> points and in the top 3 at none | [Tied ]<nth> on the map> for "<kw>"[: in Google's top 3 at <you> of <n> points]. <number 1> is number 1 with [at least ]<points>. Checked <when>."
  • Client line: On hold only: "A clean check of this search comes first." (the client reads "Check to come" as the value)
  • Task it names: map-gap unless the store is number 1
  • Client: Yes. On hold the value reads "Check to come".
  • Green Haven: map-seos-353: fail, "37 of 111 points"; map-seos-352: pass, "58 of 121 points"; map-seos-320: fail, "Not found"
map-listed

extract-v2.mjs:761-765 · Google Maps · weight practice · title "Listed at nearly every point"

  • Made when: there is a main search: the search whose phrase is the run's keyword, else the first search on file.
  • Status: pass when the store is in Google's first 20 at 90% or more of the main search's points; watch otherwise. Never fail.
  • As rules.json writes it: found / n >= 0.9 -> pass; else watch
  • Value: "[at least ]<found> of <n>" ("at least" when some not-found points carry another area's businesses in their first 20)
  • Line: "Google listed the store in its first 20 results at <found> of <n> points for "<kw>"." plus, when some not-found points are unconfirmed, a sentence that those points carry businesses from another area about <miles> miles away.
  • Client line: When points are unconfirmed: "At least <found> of the <n> points list the store in Google's first 20 results for "<kw>"."
  • Task it names: none
  • Client: Yes. On hold the value reads "Check to come".
  • Green Haven: pass, "at least 119 of 121"

extract-v2.mjs:766-770 · Google Maps · weight data · title "A map check of "{kw}" is on file"

extract-v2.mjs:771-775 · Google Maps · weight data · title "Map checks ran in opening hours"

  • Made when: the record holds at least one sweep.
  • Status: fail when any sweep finished, or (where the starter is on record) started, outside the store's posted hours that weekday, in the store's time zone, ends included; pass when every sweep finished in hours; na otherwise. A weekday with no posted hours (or no timetable) reads as unknown, not as closed, so a sweep run on a day the store does not open is neither out of hours nor held (see findings).
  • As rules.json writes it: out > 0 -> fail; all(open == true) -> pass; else na
  • Value: "<k> of <N> after hours" or "<N> of <N>"
  • Line: Per sweep: ""<kw>" ran <start> to <finish> | finished <finish> on <weekday, date>; the store's hours that day: <hours | not listed>."

3. Tasks

A task enters the list when a check opens it (section 2), and in three other ways: client-questions when reviews, links and listings were all read (extract-v2.mjs:992); one seos-* task per SEOS finding code that has a task in the record (line 993); and every task a listed task is blocked by (line 994). Each task has an owner (us, the client, the account manager, the software team), a group, a title, steps and a done-when; the client-facing ones also have a client title and a benefit. A task named by no definition stops the extractor (line 985); so does a blocked-by task that is not on the list (line 1001).

3.1 Index

"Plan" is the task's place in SALES_ORDER, the Competitor Analysis plan (only when the task was opened, is not internal and is not service_only). "Board" is its "What is missing" bucket.

map-gap

extract-v2.mjs:914-915 (L1 at 910-912) · owner us · group map

  • Title: Close the gap to <L1 number 1> for "<L1 search>" (no L1: "Close the gap to number 1 on the map")
  • Client title: Win "<L1 search>" on the map
  • Benefit (client): Number 1 for "<L1 search>" holds [at least ]<points> of <n> points; the store holds <you>.
  • Steps: (1) Set the store's listing beside <number 1>'s, line by line (Google Maps tab): ratings, photos, review velocity, ways to shop, categories. (2) Read the software's own factors for this market before changing anything: the only one that survives its control is the distance from the grid centre. (fixed text: see findings) (3) Change one thing at a time on the listing, and date each change. (4) Check both searches again in opening hours on the same grid every four weeks. (fixed text "both": see findings)
  • Done when: Number 1 for "<L1 search>", or the gap to <number 1> halved, in a check taken in opening hours.
  • Opened by: map-{search key}
  • Competitor Analysis: When opened, unless its opening check is internal (ours): plan position 2 of SALES_ORDER.
  • Note: L1 = the first loss among searches not on hold: searches with no top-3 point first, then the largest gap to number 1 as a share of the points.
  • Green Haven: task 2, status fail

4. Holds

extract-v2.mjs:1012-1041. One rule: the holds table ("Not safe to quote yet", Action Plan overview) lists exactly the numbers the client copy never prints. Each hold carries leak, the patterns (regular expressions, matched without regard to case) the client copy must not contain. A number in a pattern is written as the report prints it (thousands commas), and is not matched inside a longer number (num(), line 1019); where the bare number is also a different printable value, the pattern carries the words around it (line 1026).

The client build reads the Competitor Analysis the way a reader meets it (the text, the tooltips, labels and alt text, and the find box) and stops on any hit ("BUILD FAILED: the client copy prints a number on hold") or on a hold that names no pattern (build-report.mjs:662-674). Green Haven: 9 holds; the Action Plan shows 8 (the own-accounts hold is about our other accounts, section 6).

HoldWhereWho clears itGreen Haven
map-search-heldGoogle MapsUs: a clean check of the same searchnot raised
expected-search-missingGoogle MapsUs: find or run the checknot raised
rival-reviews-cappedNot printed in this reportSoftware team: pull every reviewraised
rival-links-partialLinks and listingsSoftware team: read every linkraised
linking-site-totalsLinks and listingsNobody: compare only the sites that are not link sellersraised
link-gap-floorLinks and listingsSoftware team: raise the limitraised
chain-whole-websiteGoogle search, Links and listingsNobody: compare one-store websites onlyraised
crawl-at-limitWebsiteSoftware team: crawl past 100 pagesraised
unconfirmed-not-foundGoogle MapsSoftware team: keep other areas out of the sweepsraised
own-accountsGoogle MapsNobody: never said to a clientraised, left out of the Action Plan
phone-named-cross-storeLinks and listingsSoftware team: answer every search for every storeraised

map-search-held

extract-v2.mjs:1020

  • Raised when: A search on file is on hold: its sweep has hold reasons (rule 1: ran outside posted hours; a far business in a top 3 changes the store's own count; the sweep's point count and its cells disagree; the rank field and the lists disagree; the share and the points disagree), or the market file and the record disagree about a search (every search goes on hold).
  • The number (as the team reads it): "<kw>": <you> of <n> points
  • Where: Google Maps
  • Why (sentence): The hold reasons, joined.
  • Who clears it: Us: a clean check of the same search
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): "<kw>"[^.]{0,80}<you> of <n> (each number as printed, not inside a longer number)
  • Green Haven: not raised

expected-search-missing

extract-v2.mjs:1021

  • Raised when: A search in settings.expected_searches has no map check on file.
  • The number (as the team reads it): Any "<kw>" result
  • Where: Google Maps
  • Why (sentence): No "<kw>" map check of this store is on file. The report says nothing about it until one is.
  • Who clears it: Us: find or run the check
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): <kw> (the phrase itself)
  • Green Haven: not raised

rival-reviews-capped

extract-v2.mjs:1022

  • Raised when: A rival's review pull stopped at the depth asked for (rule 4).
  • The number (as the team reads it): <rivals>: review count from our pull (<pulled counts>)
  • Where: Not printed in this report
  • Why (sentence): The pull stopped at the depth asked for, so it is not their count. Their ratings count on Google, and their review velocity over the windows the pull reaches back past, are printed.
  • Who clears it: Software team: pull every review
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): <pulled count> for each capped rival
  • Green Haven: raised (1)

rival-links-partial

extract-v2.mjs:1023

  • Raised when: A rival's links were not all read (the pull stopped at its page limit), so its seller count is a floor (rule 4).
  • The number (as the team reads it): Link-seller counts for <rivals> (at least <floor> among the links read)
  • Where: Links and listings
  • Why (sentence): <rival>: <read> of <total> links read. The pull stopped at its page limit, so sellers among the rest are unknown. Their linking-site totals are whole, and they are held with the other totals below.
  • Who clears it: Software team: read every link
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): <floor>[^.]{0,40}(sell|scheme)
  • Green Haven: raised (1)
