extract-v2.mjs:1024-1026

  • Raised when: Always when the store's links were read (rule 8: totals with the link sellers in mostly compare junk).
  • The number (as the team reads it): Linking-site totals: <store total> here, <rival> <total>, ...
  • Where: Links and listings
  • Why (sentence): <sellers> of this website's are link-selling or scheme pages, and the same wave reached the rivals, so the totals mostly compare junk. The report compares the classified counts.
  • Who clears it: Nobody: compare only the sites that are not link sellers
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): <store total>; for each rival with a whole total: "<total> (linking )?sites" | "linking sites[^.]{0,60}<total>" | "<rival>\W{0,3}<total>" not followed by " ratings" or " stars" and followed within 30 characters by sites, links or link
  • Green Haven: raised (1)

link-gap-floor

extract-v2.mjs:1027

  • Raised when: A part of the link-gap reading (sites that link to two or more rivals) stopped at the vendor's row limit, so the count of such sites is a floor (rule 4).
  • The number (as the team reads it): Sites that link to the rivals and not here: <k> or more
  • Where: Links and listings
  • Why (sentence): <got> of <total> and ... rows came back in two of the four parts: the vendor's limit. The total is a floor; the list of sites with some weight is read from the rows that came back. ("two of the four" is fixed text: see findings)
  • Who clears it: Software team: raise the limit
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): <k>
  • Green Haven: raised (1)

chain-whole-website

extract-v2.mjs:1028-1031

  • Raised when: Per rival whose Google listing links to an inner page (one store's page on a website for many stores): its whole-website figures are never set beside a one-store website (rule 7).
  • The number (as the team reads it): <rival>'s whole-website figures: <keywords> searches, <visits> visits a month[, link strength <rank>]
  • Where: Google search, Links and listings
  • Why (sentence): <rival>'s Google listing links to one store's page on <domain>, a website for many stores. Its whole-website figures cover every store, so they are never set beside <store>'s one-store website. The lines compare the best rival whose listing links to its own front page.
  • Who clears it: Nobody: compare one-store websites only
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): <keywords>; <visits> (the link strength named in the number has no pattern: see findings)
  • Green Haven: raised (1)

crawl-at-limit

extract-v2.mjs:1032-1033

  • Raised when: The store's site crawl stopped at its page limit (rule 4, rule 7).
  • The number (as the team reads it): Whole-site crawl counts and scores: <k> duplicate titles, <k> duplicate descriptions, score <score>; <rival> <score>, ...
  • Where: Website
  • Why (sentence): The crawl stopped at its <max>-page limit[ of the <k> pages the sitemaps list], and so did each rival's. They are counts within the first <max> pages, so no whole website leads on them.
  • Who clears it: Software team: crawl past 100 pages
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): <store score> and the same to one decimal; \d+ duplicate (titles|descriptions); on-page score, whole website; whole site: score; each rival's score and the same to one decimal
  • Green Haven: raised (1)

unconfirmed-not-found

extract-v2.mjs:1034-1036

  • Raised when: The main search's sweep has points where the store is not in the first 20 and another area's business is (rule 1, rule 5).
  • The number (as the team reads it): "<kw>": not found at <k> of <n> points
  • Where: Google Maps
  • Why (sentence): At each of those points the first 20 carries <k> businesses from another area, so the store may have been pushed out by them. The client copy says "at least <found> of <n>".
  • Who clears it: Software team: keep other areas out of the sweeps
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): (?<!at least )<found> of (the )?<n>; not found at <k>
  • Green Haven: raised (1)

own-accounts

extract-v2.mjs:1037

  • Raised when: --locations names other businesses of ours whose place is in a sweep's field.
  • The number (as the team reads it): Our own accounts on this map: <name> (business <id>), ...
  • Where: Google Maps
  • Why (sentence): They are tracked in our own software. A client hears of them only as businesses on the public map, like any rival.
  • Who clears it: Nobody: never said to a client
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): business [0-9]+; tracked in our own software; our own accounts?; (also|one of) our (clients|accounts)
  • Action Plan: left out (it matches the other-accounts pattern).
  • Green Haven: raised (1)

phone-named-cross-store

extract-v2.mjs:1038-1041

  • Raised when: Listings were read and at least one rival has a phone-with-name count (rule 9: the stores' searches were not answered alike).
  • The number (as the team reads it): Phone shown with the name, store beside store: <store> <k>, <rival> <k>, ...
  • Where: Links and listings
  • Why (sentence): The same searches were not answered alike: <store> <answered> of <asked>, <rival> ... A count over fewer answers is not a smaller footprint.
  • Who clears it: Software team: answer every search for every store
  • Leak patterns (holds[].leak, matched without regard to case): outside sites where google shows the phone with the name
  • Green Haven: raised (1)

5. Comparison rows and gap lines

5.1 Comparison rows (compare.rows)

extract-v2.mjs:1050-1161. One number, the store beside the competition. Sets: map (the businesses at the top of the run's own map check, from their Google listings) and rivals (the three stores the run names). A row reaches a client only when it is client-safe; a row that is not client-safe is marked for the team (build-report.mjs:96) and cut from the Competitor Analysis.

Every row

A row is made only when the store has a value and at least 2 entries have one. Entries run highest value first; a rival with the same value as the store comes before the store; entries with no value go last, with the reason. place and tied are given only when every entry has a value. The row reaches a client only when it is client-safe (sales and not on hold). (extract-v2.mjs:1055-1067)

  • place: if(whole, 1 + count(have_v > mine_v), null) (whole = every entry has a value); tied: whole && count(have_v == mine_v) > 1; behind: if(whole, place > 1, null).
  • Summary sentence (the first case that holds):
    • set == 'map' && mine_v == 0: top_name + ' leads with ' + top_show + '. ' + short + ' is in Google\'s top 3 at none of the points.'
    • !whole: short + ' has ' + mine_show + '; ' + if(top_is_you, 'the most of those with a number', top_name + ' leads with ' + top_show) + '.'
    • place == 1: short + ' ' + if(tied, 'shares the lead', 'leads') + '.'
    • otherwise: top_name + ' leads with ' + top_show + '. ' + short + ' is ' + if(tied, 'tied for ', '') + ord(place) + ' of ' + str(of) + '.'
  • Entry order: v == null asc, then v desc, then is_you asc.

5.2 Gap lines (gaps, "The gap to number 1")

extract-v2.mjs:1163-1199. Each line sets one of the store's numbers beside the best there is and names it.

A line is made only when both numbers exist. lead = the store is the best (a won map search) or its number is at least the best's; level = not the best and equal. deficit is a share of the larger number, negative when the store leads. The sentence depends on diff: times, count, more, or plain ("<k> <unit> short."). A floor (number 1's count rose without far businesses) prefixes "At least". (extract-v2.mjs:1165-1172)

  • lead: you_are_best || you >= best
  • level: !you_are_best && you == best
  • deficit: if(lead, -abs(you - best) / max(abs(best), abs(you), 1), (best - you) / max(abs(best), 1))
  • sentence: if(you_are_best, if(you == best, 'Level with number 2.', 'You lead by ' + fmt(show, r2(you - best)) + '.'), if(level, 'Level.', if(lead, 'You lead.', if(diff == 'times', if(you == 0, fmt(show, best) + ' to none.', if(you <= 2 && best / you >= 10, fmt(show, best) + ' to ' + fmt(show, you) + '.', if(best / you >= 1.5, str(r1(best / you)) + ' times yours.', n(r2(best - you)) + ' more than you.'))), if(diff == 'count', n(best - you) + ' to go.', if(diff == 'more', fmt(show, r2(best - you)) + ' more than yours.', fmt(show, r2(best - you)) + ' ' + unit + ' short.'))))))
  • floor: if(floor && !lead, 'At least ' + lower_first(body), body)
  • printed numbers: fmt(show, you), fmt(show, best) (show: n = thousands commas; fixed1 = one decimal; round_n = rounded, then commas)

6. The two cuts

One model, two documents:

node build-report.mjs green-haven/report-data.json <out>/competitor-analysis.html --audience=client --doc="Competitor Analysis"
node build-report.mjs green-haven/report-data.json <out>/action-plan.html --audience=service --doc="Action Plan"

build-report.mjs first builds one page with both views (data-only="sales" and data-only="service" blocks), then cuts one view out of the file itself (cut(), lines 616-629: each element carrying the attribute is removed with everything inside it). Without --audience (internal) both views stay, with a switch.

6.1 Client audience: the Competitor Analysis

What is cut (build-report.mjs:631-636): every element marked data-only="service" or data-team. That removes the team overview (task cards, the holds table, "Since the last report", health by area), the team's check rows and the data-check blocks, the "Tasks here" lists, the team notes on cards, every comparison card that is not client-safe (line 96), every gap line on hold (line 138), the "Not compared yet" lists (line 102), the store picker, the Present button and the Sales / Service switch. The AI tab button and its content are service-only (lines 452, 587); the empty AI section is then removed (line 633) and the find box lists no AI tab (line 642). The find box keeps only items not marked service (line 634); no task data, no seller list and no run id go into the file (lines 635, 642-643).

The leak gate (build-report.mjs:652-661). The page body, with the stylesheet and the inline script taken out (the find box data stays in), must not contain any of: a service block (data-only="service"); a team-only block (data-internal); the view switch (data-mode-set); the words "software team" or "on hold"; when the main map check is on hold, its map shares and the map check card (id="scan"); the name of a tool we use (Local Falcon, localrankingtracker, lf-static, DataForSEO, Eagle Eyes); the id of a comparison card kept for the team; the "not compared yet" list (id="cmp-missing-); a collection limit ("pull's limit", "the pull stops"); our own tag (utm_, or the listing's utm_source value); the run id; a low-star review quote (data-quote); task internals ("steps", done_when). One hit: "BUILD FAILED: the client copy still carries: ...". Then the held-numbers gate (section 4).

6.2 Service audience: the Action Plan

The other-accounts cut (build-report.mjs:27-44). Every check, task and hold whose JSON matches XACCT is left out of the document:

\bbusiness [0-9]+\b|tracked in our own software|\bour own accounts?\b|(also|one of) our (clients|accounts)|another account

(without regard to case). Each one left out is printed ("left out of the service document (about our other accounts): ...", line 688).

  • Orphan gate (lines 38-40): the build stops when a kept task is blocked by a task left out, a kept check names a task left out, or a plan item names a task left out. Two of its tests read fields the model does not have (t.check, p.task), so they never fire; see the known defects.
  • Count gate (lines 41-42): the build stops when a check left out is not a data check and its area is counted in the tiles (the tiles would then count a check the document does not show).
  • The task group counts are recounted (line 43).
  • Then every data-only="sales" and data-team element is cut (line 639): the client headline, the client tiles, "What is missing", the client's check rows, "What we would do here", the client plan and the view switch; the find box drops its sales-only items (line 640). The team-only blocks (data-internal) stay: this is the team's document. Its Present button hides team notes, numbers on hold and software-team work while a client can see the screen (line 582).
  • The gate (lines 676-686): the document, read the way a reader meets it, must hold no Sales-only block, no view switch and nothing matching XACCT. One hit: "BUILD FAILED: the service document still carries: ...".

Green Haven (rebuilt in this session, the builder's own output): left out own-accounts (check), answer-scope (check), answer-isolation (task) and the own-accounts hold. Both rebuilt documents are byte-identical to green-haven/docs/.

6.3 The --doc name

--doc="<name>" (build-report.mjs:24, trimmed) names the document in four places: the browser title "<short name> <city> · <name>" (line 573, in place of "SEO health report"), the header (line 579), the client overview's first line (line 232, in place of "SEO and competition report") and the team overview's first line (line 277, in place of "Service view"). Green Haven: "Green Haven Elizabeth · Competitor Analysis" and "Green Haven Elizabeth · Action Plan".

6.4 The find box

On every audience, every place the find box can send a reader must exist on the page, or the build stops ("the find box points at places that are not on the page", build-report.mjs:648-651).

7. The 10 client-report rules and the code that enforces them

The ten rules at the top of extract-v2.mjs (lines 20-34).

#RuleEnforced byOn a breach
1A number that rests on a flawed reading is on hold: shown to the team with the reason and who clears it, never quoted to a client, never leaned on by the headline.Sweep tests extract-v2.mjs:225-231: out of posted hours (226), a far business that changes the store's own count (227), points against cells (228), rank field against lists (229), share against points (230). Market file against record: every search on hold (306-317). The map check goes na with a client line (753, 759). The headline, L1 and the gap lines use searches not on hold only (1204, 910, 1173). The hold row and its leak pattern (1020). The held-numbers gate (build-report.mjs:662-674).A held number in the client copy stops the build. A held search never heads the page.
2Evidence that carries the agency's own tag is ours: team only.isOurs (extract-v2.mjs:142-143); listing-tag and directory-work checks are internal (797, 871); SEOS evidence links carrying our tag are never shown (966-967); listing rows flag ours (684). Gate: nothing a client can see carries utm_<x>=<agency> (1247-1248). Client leak gate: utm_ or the listing's tag (build-report.mjs:660)."EXTRACT FAILED: a line a client can see carries our own tag", or BUILD FAILED.
3The client copy is a separate file.--audience=client (build-report.mjs:21-23), the cut (631-636), the leak gate (652-661).BUILD FAILED: the client copy still carries ...
4A count that stopped at a collection limit is not printed as the count.Review pulls: count null when capped (extract-v2.mjs:323-332, 390). Links: seller counts null when the links were not all read (513, 525). Link gap: "or more" and a floor (556, 585, 1027). Crawl: at the limit (447). Holds 1022, 1023, 1027, 1032-1033 with leak patterns; the crawl-score card is team-only (1118). Client leak gate: "pull's limit" (build-report.mjs:659).A held count in the client copy stops the build. Elsewhere by construction (no count is computed).
5An empty read is "could not be read", never "not there".Listing rows say "nothing: the page came back empty" (extract-v2.mjs:635); verdicts say "Could not be read" (647); "Not checked in this report" (648); the check lines (879, 881); not-found points with far businesses are "at least" and held (761-765, 1034-1036).By construction only; no gate checks the wording (the unconfirmed not-found hold has leak patterns).
6Map points are counted from each sweep's own cells: "58 of 121 points".Counting from each point's first 20 (extract-v2.mjs:196-205); the value "<k> of <n> points" (758). When the rank field, the lists or the share disagree the sweep goes on hold (228-230) and scan-depth fails (783-785). Line 1250 only prints a note.The sweep is held (not quoted) and the data check fails; the build does not stop.
7Whole-website figures are labelled as whole-website figures.Rows scoped "Whole website" (extract-v2.mjs:1098-1099, 1118, 1123, 1126-1133); gap lines scoped whole (1192-1195) and drawn with a "Whole websites" chip (build-report.mjs:139). A chain rival's figures are never set beside the store (398, 1096-1097, 1190-1191) and are held (1029-1031).A held chain figure in the client copy stops the build. The labels themselves are not gated.
8Linking-site totals are classified first (link sellers and scheme pages out), then counted.The seller and network classification (extract-v2.mjs:488-534); the client line of linking-sites gives only classified counts (866-867); the totals hold (1024-1026); the totals card is held (1131).A total in the client copy stops the build.
9Say what the tool saw; two fields of one reading that disagree are "not confirmed".On-page score (extract-v2.mjs:442-443, card 1116); main-heading (834-835); store-details (840-842); review velocity against SEOS's snapshots (377-379, 811-812, 1086); speed order quoted only when both readings give it (1105-1110, build-report.mjs:472); phone-with-name counts held (1040-1041, 1138-1140, 1199).By construction (the check reads "Not confirmed", goes na or is held); no general gate.
10The owner's ordering: losing first, winning last (meta.order = 'loss-first').extract-v2.mjs:739-740, 910, 1201-1218, 1349; build-report.mjs:54-56, 99-100, 109, 134, 146, 186-188. Gate: the headline names the biggest loss (1252)."EXTRACT FAILED: the headline does not lead with the biggest loss". The other orders hold by construction; check-rules.mjs verifies them.

Two more gates in extract-v2.mjs serve the same rules: a result claimed for an expected search that is not on file stops the build (line 1254), and with --facts every number the model shares with the independent facts file must agree (lines 1256-1340; RUN.md records 185 shared numbers, 0 disagreeing, on 2026-10-12).

8. Known defects and non-generic spots

Reported, not fixed (the reference code stays as it is). Each is in parts/C2-rules.json with a proposed fix. The ones printed in the Green Haven documents were seen in those files; two others were shown by running the code on copies (marked "shown"); the rest are read from the code and not verified by running it.

  • Printed now in the Green Haven Action Plan: map-gap step 4 says "Check both searches again" with three searches on file (extract-v2.mjs:915); the map checks note says "A far-away business in a point's top 3 would put that check on hold" while "weed near me" has one in a top 3 at 66 points and is not held, because the code holds only when the store's own count changes (build-report.mjs:387 against extract-v2.mjs:227; the header comment at lines 23-24 says the same as the note); the "What was read, and when" table prints full times for the map checks because a pattern lacks its backslashes (build-report.mjs:565).
  • Would misfire for another business: a vertical other than Cannabis gets category na but still opens fix-category, which reaches the client's plan (extract-v2.mjs:789-791; shown by running the extractor with a copy of the settings file whose vertical is "Vape shop": "Set the right main category" became plan item 6); listing-link names a task town-page that is not defined (extract-v2.mjs:796; inert while one store is built); stored-findings with findings but no tasks names no task, so its find-box link fails the build (extract-v2.mjs:892, build-report.mjs:546, 651; shown on a model copy: "BUILD FAILED: the find box points at places that are not on the page: tk-null"); a weekday with no posted hours reads as unknown, so a map check run on a day the store does not open is neither out of hours nor held (extract-v2.mjs:159, used at 216 and 226); the expected-search gate builds a pattern from the phrase without escaping it (extract-v2.mjs:1254; the agency name likewise at 1248); fixed text in task steps: "for Elizabeth and the towns around it" (926), "(11 by 11, 2 miles)" (916), "Fix the duplicate meta tags" (925), "Search Console is not connected" (932), "the only one that survives its control is the distance from the grid centre" (915), "the first 100 pages" (946, 1032), "two of the four parts" (1027), "the three rivals" (869-870, build-report.mjs:515, 527), "its Council Bluffs vantage" (779); rescan-open-hours uses Monday's hours for every day (917); connected says "Neither is connected" when one of the two is (820).
  • Cannabis-specific: CATEGORY (789), the low-star subjects ("budtender", "bad weed": 335-340), the name shortener (108), the age-gate heading (455), CANNABIS_SITE (492) and its "Cannabis directory" chip (build-report.mjs:515), the directories that matter (Weedmaps, Leafly, Dutchie: 594-595), the client email's directories (918), "<city> dispensary" (283), "cannabis articles" (865), "cannabis ones" and "cannabis sites" in task steps (928, 930).
  • Rule edges: the phone speed band reads the raw score while the page prints it rounded (a raw 0.895 prints 90 and is "Needs a look"; extract-v2.mjs:431, 435); the three loss orders differ in their tie-breaks (739, 910, 1205); the chain hold names a link strength its leak patterns do not cover (1030-1031); the orphan gate reads t.check and p.task, which the model never has (build-report.mjs:38-39); title names no task even when it is watch (837); review-count passes when the store beats the smallest of the stores beside it (799; Green Haven's smallest has 6 ratings); the map's subtitle says "every one taken in opening hours" whenever no check is known to be outside them, including checks whose hours are unknown (build-report.mjs:115); the find box's search words for the listing link include "charlotte", a town from another report (build-report.mjs:219).
  • Comments that disagree with the code: the Compare switch is said to be off in the Service view (build-report.mjs:12-13) but opens on in both (client.js:50-53); the compare sets name a "nearby" set no row uses (extract-v2.mjs:1051-1053); rival-rows carries a pass wording that can never be emitted (891); DATA-NOTES.md (section 5, rule 10) still says "lead with what they built", the opposite of the code's loss-first rule.

9. How this was checked

Run from Product/seos-report/ on 2026-10-12 with Node 24.15.0:

node handoff/seos-report-handoff-v1/contract/check-rules.mjs green-haven/report-data.json \
  --md=handoff/seos-report-handoff-v1/contract/RULES.md \
  --client-doc=green-haven/docs/competitor-analysis.html \
  --service-doc=green-haven/docs/action-plan.html

Result: PASS, 940 of 940. What that covers:

  • Ids: all 43 checks, 34 tasks, 9 holds, 24 comparison rows and 15 gap lines of the Green Haven model have their rule in rules.json (50 check rules, 33 task rules, 11 holds, 22 comparison rows and 14 gap lines, families counted once).
  • Check statuses: 34 recomputed from the model's own values with the rule as rules.json writes it; 8 fixed by their rule (always watch, fail or na); 1 not evaluable from the model (answer-scope: the counts it rests on are not in report-data.json). 41 value lines recomputed. 45 presence rules tested: a check the rules say is made is in the model, and one they say is not made is absent.
  • Tasks: owner, group, opening checks, status, ours flag and blocked-by for all 34; the 10-item plan against SALES_ORDER; the task numbers 1 to 34; the task group counts.
  • Holds: 9, each matched by its "clears" line, each with valid leak patterns.
  • Comparison rows: 24: client-safe and on-hold flags, key flag, place, tie, the summary sentence and the entry order.
  • Gap lines: 15: lead, level, deficit, the sentence and the printed numbers; 19 of their numbers traced back to the model.
  • Orders: the map searches (loss first), the headline's losses, wins and both lines, the area tile counts.
  • The documents: which checks each one shows and their order on each tab, the Wrong / To look at / Right board, the gap lines, the comparison cards, the plan and its buckets, the holds table (8 rows), the task list (33 tasks).
  • The snapshot: the 130 Green Haven entries in rules.json agree with the model.
  • RULES.md names every rule id in rules.json.

The checker can fail. Seventeen deliberate breaks, each made on a copy (a status flipped; a threshold changed in rules.json; an unknown check id; number 1's points lowered; an unknown hold; the plan reordered; a team-only row marked client-safe; a deficit; a value; an owner; the headline; a tile count; a missing check; the search order; a summary; a stray opening check; two gap lines swapped in the Competitor Analysis) were all caught, each in the area expected.

The two documents were also rebuilt from the model into a scratch folder with the commands in section 6: both are byte-identical to green-haven/docs/ (sha256 fd7a98cc... for the Competitor Analysis, 3e599768... for the Action Plan), and the builder reported the four items it left out of the Action Plan.

Wording

All 247 sentence templates and fixed phrases

contract/WORDING.md 129 KB

The wording of the two documents

Generated by contract/check-wording.mjs from contract/wording.json after it proved every entry; do not edit by hand. Each entry is a fixed phrase or a sentence template the documents are written from: where it shows, the template with {slots}, what each slot reads from report-data.json, what selects the wording, the code that writes it, and the Green Haven example.

Result of the run that wrote this file: 212 entries verified (rendered from Green Haven values read from report-data.json and found verbatim in a document or in the model), 35 marked "not exercised by the Green Haven data". 371 example values were read back from the model by their paths; 41 are literals (the --doc name and constants).

Scope: Green Haven Industries (SEOS business 48, Elizabeth NJ), meta.v2 = true, meta.order = loss-first. build-report.mjs also holds wording for the older High Society file (meta.v2 absent): those branches are inert when meta.v2 is true and are not listed. Sources: the fixed words and the sentence shapes live in build-report.mjs (the page), mapview.js (the map, drawn in the file and again in the page) and extract-v2.mjs (every sentence stored in the model: the verdict, check, task, hold, gap and comparison text). The build prints model strings as they are, escaped. Readable text: what check-wording.mjs matches against is the document with style and script blocks removed, tags turned to spaces, entities decoded, and the text of tooltips and labels (data-tip, aria-label, title, placeholder, alt) kept. A match found only in a tooltip or label says so.

How a template is written

  • {slot} prints the example value as it is. {slot|format} and {slot|format:arg:arg} apply one of the formats below (the same rules the code uses).
  • slots says which model key fills each slot; example_slots holds the Green Haven values; example_paths names, for each slot, the path in report-data.json the value was read from (a.b[0], [key=value] for the first match, [*key=value] for every match, len(), map(list, key), [x, y], x - y, x + y). A value that is not stored in the model (the --doc name, a word picked by a condition) is marked literal: with the reason.
  • condition is what selects the wording; source is the file, line and function; source_probe is text on that line (check-wording.mjs --src checks it).
  • status is "verified" (check-wording.mjs proved it this run) or "not exercised by the Green Haven data" (a branch these documents do not show; not counted as verified).

The headline and its lead (the verdict rule)

extract-v2.mjs works out verdict.a, verdict.b and verdict.lead from the searches not on hold (maps.searches). Losses are the searches the store does not lead: those with no top-3 point first, then by the share of points behind number 1. Wins are the searches it leads, by margin over number 2. verdict.a = the first loss's head (or the first win's when nothing is lost); verdict.b = the first win's head when there are losses and wins, else the second loss's head, else empty. The lead is every loss line, then every win line, then the ratings line. With no usable search the three no-search entries apply. The build stops if the headline does not lead with the biggest loss (extract-v2.mjs:1252).

verdict.loss-head.nowhere

  • Where: verdict.a: the Overview headline (h1, Sales) and the Google Maps tab headline (both views)
  • Template: Nowhere for "{kw}".
  • Slots: kw = the search of the biggest loss, verdict.losses[0] (a maps.searches[].kw)
  • Shown when: The biggest loss has no point in Google's top 3 (you = 0) and is in no point's first 20 (found = 0). Losses run: searches with no top-3 point first, then by the share of points behind number 1, biggest first.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1207 lossHead
  • Example: "Nowhere for "weed near me"."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

verdict.loss-head.outside

  • Where: verdict.a (or verdict.b for a second loss)
  • Template: Outside the top 3 for "{kw}".
  • Slots: kw = the loss's maps.searches[].kw
  • Shown when: The loss has no top-3 point (you = 0) but Google lists the store lower down at one point or more (found > 0).
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1207 lossHead
  • Example: none: not exercised by the Green Haven data.

verdict.loss-head.place

  • Where: verdict.a (or verdict.b for a second loss)
  • Template: {place|placeword} for "{kw}".
  • Slots: place = maps.searches[].place, the store's place by top-3 points; kw = maps.searches[].kw
  • Shown when: The loss has top-3 points (you > 0). verdict.b takes it only when there is no win.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1207 lossHead
  • Example: none: not exercised by the Green Haven data.
  • Note: With Green Haven's data the second loss (Third for "cannabis near me".) is not printed: verdict.b takes the win.

verdict.win-head.by

  • Where: verdict.b (verdict.a when nothing is lost)
  • Template: First for "{kw}", by {margin|plural:point:points}.
  • Slots: kw = the best win, verdict.wins[0]; margin = maps.searches[].you - maps.searches[].second_points of that search
  • Shown when: The store is number 1 for the search and ahead of number 2 by 1 or 2 points. Wins run by margin over number 2, as a share of the points, biggest first.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1208 winHead
  • Example: "First for "dispensary near me", by 1 point."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

verdict.win-head.first

  • Where: verdict.b (verdict.a when nothing is lost)
  • Template: First for "{kw}".
  • Slots: kw = the best win, verdict.wins[0]
  • Shown when: Number 1 by more than 2 points.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1208 winHead
  • Example: none: not exercised by the Green Haven data.

verdict.win-head.tied

  • Where: verdict.b (verdict.a when nothing is lost)
  • Template: Tied first for "{kw}".
  • Slots: kw = the best win, verdict.wins[0]
  • Shown when: The store leads with as many points as number 2 (margin 0).
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1208 winHead
  • Example: none: not exercised by the Green Haven data.

verdict.loss-line.none

  • Where: verdict.lead: under the Overview headline (Sales)
  • Template: For "{kw}" {short} is not in Google's top 3 at any of the {n} map points, and not in the first 20 at any of them; {leader}, at number 1, holds {floor|if:at least }{leader_points}.
  • Slots: kw = maps.searches[].kw; short = business.short; n = maps.searches[].n (points in the check); leader = maps.searches[].leader; floor = maps.searches[].leader_floor (number 1's count is a floor: another area's business sat in a top 3); leader_points = maps.searches[].leader_points
  • Shown when: A loss with you = 0 and found = 0.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1209 lossLine
  • Example: "For "weed near me" Green Haven is not in Google's top 3 at any of the 121 map points, and not in the first 20 at any of them; Joyleaf, at number 1, holds at least 117."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, report-data.json

verdict.loss-line.lower

  • Where: verdict.lead
  • Template: For "{kw}" {short} is not in Google's top 3 at any of the {n} map points, though Google lists it lower down at {found}; {leader}, at number 1, holds {floor|if:at least }{leader_points}.
  • Slots: kw = maps.searches[].kw; short = business.short; n = maps.searches[].n; found = maps.searches[].found; leader = maps.searches[].leader; floor = maps.searches[].leader_floor; leader_points = maps.searches[].leader_points
  • Shown when: A loss with you = 0 and found > 0.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1209 lossLine
  • Example: none: not exercised by the Green Haven data.

verdict.loss-line.placed

  • Where: verdict.lead
  • Template: For "{kw}" {short} is {tied|if:tied }{place|placeword_lower}, in Google's top 3 at {you} of {n} map points; {leader}, at number 1, holds {leader_points}.
  • Slots: kw = maps.searches[].kw; short = business.short; tied = maps.searches[].tied; place = maps.searches[].place; you = maps.searches[].you; n = maps.searches[].n; leader = maps.searches[].leader; leader_points = maps.searches[].leader_points
  • Shown when: A loss with top-3 points (you > 0).
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1210 lossLine
  • Example: "For "cannabis near me" Green Haven is third, in Google's top 3 at 37 of 111 map points; Zen Leaf, at number 1, holds 88."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, report-data.json
  • Note: This line has no "at least": a number 1 whose count is a floor (leader_floor) prints as a plain count here, unlike the loss line with no points and the Google Maps tab lead. See findings.

verdict.win-line

  • Where: verdict.lead
  • Template: For "{kw}" {who} is number 1, at {you} of {n} points, {margin|plural:point:points} ahead of {second} at {second_points}.
  • Slots: kw = maps.searches[].kw; who = business.short for the first win when nothing is lost, else "it"; you = maps.searches[].you; n = maps.searches[].n; margin = you - second_points; second = maps.searches[].second; second_points = maps.searches[].second_points
  • Shown when: A win whose margin over number 2 is 1 point or more.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1211 winLine
  • Example: "For "dispensary near me" it is number 1, at 58 of 121 points, 1 point ahead of Zen Leaf at 57."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, report-data.json

verdict.win-line.level

  • Where: verdict.lead

  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1211 winLine
  • Example: none: not exercised by the Green Haven data.

The map, point by point (build-report.mjs and mapview.js)

mapview.js draws the first view into the file and redraws it in the page on every pick, so the printed words and the redrawn words come from one function.

map.sub

  • Where: under "The map, point by point"
  • Template: Each dot is a spot around town where we searched Google Maps, and the number is the place Google gave the store there. {reports|n} checks of {searches} searches since {first}, every one taken in opening hours.
  • Slots: reports = map.reports; searches = map.searches.length; first = map.first
  • Shown when: map.outside_hours is 0; otherwise the end reads "{outside_hours} of them outside opening hours".
  • Source: build-report.mjs:115 mapPortal
  • Example: "Each dot is a spot around town where we searched Google Maps, and the number is the place Google gave the store there. 3 checks of 3 searches since Oct 11, 2026, every one taken in opening hours."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan

map.line.behind

  • Where: the sentence over the two grids (Compare on)
  • Template: {vs} holds {them} of {n} points. {me} holds {you}.
  • Slots: vs = the business beside the store (number 1 by default); them = its top-3 points; n = points in the check; me = business.short; you = the store's top-3 points
  • Shown when: The business beside the store has more points; " That is {times} times as many." follows when the store has points and the ratio is 1.5 or more.
  • Source: mapview.js:141 line
  • Example: "Joyleaf holds 117 of 121 points. Green Haven holds 0."

The gap to number 1

gaps[].text is written by gap() in extract-v2.mjs: the comparator is number 1 on the map, the best rival, Google's mark or a target; diff "times", "count" or "more" picks the wording; a floor adds "At least".

gaps.sub

  • Where: under "The gap to number 1"
  • Template: Each line sets {short} beside the best there is and names it. Biggest gaps first, and the lines where the store is level or ahead are at the end.
  • Slots: short = business.short
  • Shown when: gaps is not empty (Compare on).
  • Source: build-report.mjs:142 gapSection
  • Example: "Each line sets Green Haven beside the best there is and names it. Biggest gaps first, and the lines where the store is level or ahead are at the end."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan

gaps.who

  • Where: each gap line, under its label
  • Template: {who}: {best_name}
  • Slots: who = gaps[].who; best_name = gaps[].best_name (left out when it is "You")
  • Shown when: Always.
  • Source: build-report.mjs:139 gapLine
  • Example: "Number 1 on the map: Joyleaf"
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan

gaps.text.floor-none

  • Where: gap line text (gaps[].text)
  • Template: At least {best|n} to none.
  • Slots: best = gaps[].best
  • Shown when: diff "times", the store has 0, and number 1's count is a floor (leader_floor): the text gets "At least " and a small first letter.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1169 gap
  • Example: "At least 117 to none."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

gaps.text.times

  • Where: gap line text
  • Template: {ratio} times yours.
  • Slots: ratio = gaps[].best / gaps[].you, to 1 decimal
  • Shown when: diff "times", best / yours 1.5 or more (and not the "to" case).
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1169 gap
  • Example: "2.4 times yours."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

gaps.text.pair

  • Where: gap line text
  • Template: {best} to {mine}.
  • Slots: best = gaps[].best_show; mine = gaps[].you_show
  • Shown when: diff "times", yours 2 or less and best 10 times yours or more.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1169 gap
  • Example: none: not exercised by the Green Haven data.
  • Fits other text: Competitor Analysis: "6 to 3,259." (the review-count check detail ends "have 6 to 3,259.", the same shape)

gaps.text.more-than-you

  • Where: gap line text
  • Template: {d|n} more than you.
  • Slots: d = gaps[].best - gaps[].you
  • Shown when: diff "times", best / yours under 1.5.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1169 gap
  • Example: none: not exercised by the Green Haven data.

gaps.text.to-go

  • Where: gap line text
  • Template: {d|n} to go.
  • Slots: d = gaps[].best - gaps[].you
  • Shown when: diff "count".
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1170 gap
  • Example: "42 to go."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

gaps.text.more

  • Where: gap line text
  • Template: {d|n} more than yours.
  • Slots: d = gaps[].best - gaps[].you
  • Shown when: diff "more".
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1170 gap
  • Example: "343 more than yours."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

gaps.text.short

  • Where: gap line text
  • Template: {d|n} {unit} short.
  • Slots: d = gaps[].best - gaps[].you; unit = the line's unit (points)
  • Shown when: No diff kind given (the default).
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1170 gap
  • Example: "67 points short."

gaps.text.lead-by

  • Shown when: The store is number 1 on the map for the search.

  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

gaps.text.lead

gaps.text.level

A check row prints checks[].title, checks[].value and checks[].detail (a client reads checks[].sales when the check has one, and "Check to come" in place of a value on hold). The check ids and their full wording are listed by another part of this package; the entries here are the row's shape and a few checks as examples.

Task cards, plan items and groups

A task card prints tasks[].n and tasks[].title, then chips: the owner (Us, The client, Account manager, Software team), tasks[].group_label, the status chip, "Ours" when internal, "Blocked by task N" and "New this run". Opened: Why (tasks[].why), Steps (tasks[].steps), Done when (tasks[].done_when), Blocked by. Task titles, steps and done-when lines are written in extract-v2.mjs TASKS (lines 913-952).

  • Where: the owner chip of a task card
  • Template: {owner}
  • Slots: owner = OWNER[tasks[].owner]: Us, The client, Account manager, Software team

Comparison cards

A card prints compare.rows[].label, the On hold chip when held, compare.rows[].summary, a bar per entry (or the entry's reason in place of a bar), the scope chip (Map check, This store, Whole website, Store page) and compare.rows[].note; the team note is Service only. Labels, summaries and notes are written by cmpRow() in extract-v2.mjs.

compare.panel

  • Where: the heading of every comparison panel
  • Template: You and the competition
  • Shown when: Every tab, Compare on.
  • Source: build-report.mjs:103 cmpPanel
  • Example: "You and the competition"
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan

compare.summary.place

  • Where: a comparison card's summary (compare.rows[].summary)
  • Template: {top} leads with {show}. {short} is {tied|if:tied for }{place|ord} of {k}.
  • Slots: top = the entry with the most; show = its value as shown; short = business.short; tied = compare.rows[].tied; place = compare.rows[].place; k = compare.rows[].of
  • Shown when: Every entry has a number and the store is not first.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1063 cmpRow
  • Example: "Budzooka leads with 6,310. Green Haven is 6th of 7."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

compare.summary.leads

  • Where: a comparison card's summary
  • Template: {short} leads.
  • Slots: short = business.short
  • Shown when: Every entry has a number and the store is first alone; "{short} shares the lead." when tied.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1063 cmpRow
  • Example: "Green Haven leads."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

compare.summary.shares

  • Where: a comparison card's summary
  • Template: {short} shares the lead.
  • Slots: short = business.short
  • Shown when: The store is first, tied.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1063 cmpRow
  • Example: "Green Haven shares the lead."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

compare.summary.partial

  • Where: a comparison card's summary when an entry has no number
  • Template: {short} has {mine}; {top} leads with {show}.
  • Slots: short = business.short; mine = the store's value as shown; top = the entry with the most; show = its value
  • Shown when: Some entry has no number and the store is not the most.
  • Source: extract-v2.mjs:1063 cmpRow
  • Example: "Green Haven has 122; Budzooka leads with 465."
  • Verified: found in Competitor Analysis, Action Plan, report-data.json

compare.summary.partial-most

  • Where: a comparison card's summary when an entry has no number
  • Template: {short} has {mine}; the most of those with a number.
  • Slots: short = business.short; mine = the store's value as shown
  • Shown when: Some entry has no number and the store has the most.

Formatting rules for numbers and text, each with a phrase from the documents

format.ordinal-place

format.thousands

  • Where: every count over 999 (n(), en-US)

  • Slots: read = a count; total = a count

format.points

format.floor

format.stars

  • Template: {rating|fixed1} stars

format.month

What was scrubbed from this fixture

Written by scrub.mjs (mode stub) from the SEOS answers in green-haven-2026-10-12 (business 48). Counts and kinds only: no removed value appears here.

Removed

business-48.json

  • table analytics_sync: 0 rows (the name marks tokens, credentials or account links; no script in the chain names it)
  • table analytics_sync_runs: 0 rows (the name marks tokens, credentials or account links; no script in the chain names it)
  • table portal_access: 0 rows (the name marks tokens, credentials or account links; no script in the chain names it)
  • table portal_tokens: 1 row (the name marks tokens, credentials or account links; no script in the chain names it)
  • column notifications.dedupe_key: removed from 4 rows (the name holds "key"; no script in the chain names it)
  • column vendor_spend.step_key: removed from 804 rows (the name holds "key"; no script in the chain names it)
  • the answer's counts header still lists the removed tables with their row counts, and its not_included list names some of them, as SEOS sent it: names and counts only

full-audit-48.json

  • 4 Google Analytics and Search Console readings about 2 places that are not the store (2 analytics_watch, 2 gsc_sitemaps): request and result set to null and endpoints emptied, 5,755 bytes in all. Each row keeps every other field (its kind, place id, website address, vendor, cost and fetch time, and its empty errors and notes), because the report's own check that SEOS mixes another account's readings into this answer (check answer-scope, task answer-isolation, both team-only and left out of the Action Plan) counts them and names their websites. The store's own analytics readings kept: 0.

locations-all.json

  • 41 of 54 rows removed; 13 kept: 3 are our other accounts in a sweep's field (what extract-v2.mjs --locations reads), 12 are the subjects of SEOS's "weed" sweeps (what oracle/gh-facts.mjs measures the nearest such sweep from), 2 are both. The file's total field is left as SEOS sent it (54).

input/extra-ee/eagleeyes-scan-320-weed-near-me.json

  • the scan machine's network address and provider (request.vantage.ip, request.vantage.isp) set to null: 2 fields. The chain reads only request.vantage.label (ee-scan-to-seos.mjs:73). Every other byte is as Eagle Eyes wrote it, and the file keeps the export's file time.

E-mail addresses of SEOS console users (every file)

  • 2 addresses held as whole values (who started a run, fetched a reading, set a keyword, sent a task): 973 values in 5 files (815 in input/business-48.json, 135 in input/full-audit-48.json, 14 in input/website-audit-48.json, 1 in input/business_info-history-green-haven.json, 8 in input/locations-all.json), each address replaced by a stable placeholder, person-<n>@example.invalid, numbered in the order first met. The chain reads only whether such a field is filled (sweeps-market.mjs: !!actor.username).

  • input/engine_sweep_businesses-green-haven-anywhere.json (1,335 bytes)

  "short": "Green Haven",

contract/business-settings.schema.json

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "business-settings.schema.json",
  "title": "Business settings for extract-v2.mjs --settings",
  "description": "What the SEOS record does not carry about one business, as one JSON file per business. extract-v2.mjs reads it with --settings=<file> (function settingsFrom, extract-v2.mjs lines 72-83) in place of its hard-coded SETTINGS table. This schema states exactly what settingsFrom accepts today, including a few loose spots that are marked 'accepted today' in a key's description and listed as findings in parts/B-contract.json. Every failure stops the build with 'EXTRACT FAILED: <message>' and exit code 1. The one exception: a file whose content is the JSON value null crashes with 'TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object' (still exit code 1). Without --settings the extractor falls back to its SETTINGS table (businesses 26 and 48 only), and an unknown business silently gets no settings at all.",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "business_id"
  ],
  "dependentRequired": {
    "other_market_sources": [
      "other_market_label"
    ]
  },
  "properties": {
    "$schema": {
      "description": "Not read. Any value is accepted (it is only on the list of known keys)."
    },
    "note": {
      "description": "Not read. Any value is accepted. For people: what the file is and why it exists."
    },
    "business_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Which business the file is for. Required. It must be the same number as businesses[0].id in the business answer (GET /api/data/v1/businesses/{id}), compared with ===. Missing or different: 'the settings file is for business <x>, not <id>'. A quoted number such as \"48\" also fails, with the confusing message 'the settings file is for business 48, not 48'. Not written into the report."
    },
    "brand": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "\\S",
      "description": "The store's name as Google shows it. A fallback only: business.name is the Google listing's title first (business_info reading), then brand, then the register name (businesses.name); business.short is short first, then brand. Green Haven: removing it changes nothing (the listing has a title and short is set). Must hold a character other than white space, else 'settings.brand must be a non-empty string' (null fails the same way)."
    },
    "short": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "\\S",
      "description": "The short name the two documents use in sentences, tiles, tables and comparisons (business.short, you.short, the store's own entry on every comparison card, the headline lines, checks, gap lines and the plan; also the store's key in links.quality.strict). Without it: brand, else the register name with words like ' Dispensary' cut off (shortName). Green Haven: removing it makes the short name 'Green Haven Industries' and changes both documents. Must hold a character other than white space."
    },
    "brand_terms": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string",
        "pattern": "\\S"
      },
      "description": "The store's name and close spellings, matched case-insensitively with any white space inside a term optional. (1) A ranked search that contains one is a brand search (search.stored_brand and stored_plain; needs the ranked_keywords reading, which Green Haven's run did not have). (2) A linking site with weight whose page title contains one is 'names the store' (links.quality, the linking-sites check). Each item must hold a character other than white space, and the value must be a list, else 'settings.brand_terms must be a list of non-empty strings'. // run-report.mjs: one command from SEOS's answers to the two documents, on the reference code in reference/.
// Every stage is a child process on a reference script; the first stage that exits non-zero stops the run.
//
// usage: node run-report.mjs --data=<folder> --settings=<file> --out=<folder> [--extra-sweep=<Eagle Eyes export>]...
//          [--facts=<file>] [--no-browser]
//   --data         the answers of SEOS's GETs: business-<id>.json (/businesses/{id}), full-audit-<id>.json
//                  (/businesses/{id}/full-audit-result), website-audit-<id>.json (/businesses/{id}/website-audit-result) and,
//                  when present, engine_sweeps-all.json (/tables/engine_sweeps) and locations-all.json (/tables/locations).
//                  Never written to.
//   --settings     the business settings (extract-v2.mjs --settings): business_id is required and names the answers.
//   --out          an empty or new folder. Gets market.json, report-data.json, competitor-analysis.html,
//                  action-plan.html, SHA256SUMS, run-log.txt, logs/ (each stage's output) and, with an extra sweep,
//                  data/ (the answers with the sweep folded in) and extra/ (the converted sweep).
//   --extra-sweep  an Eagle Eyes scan export of the store: converted to SEOS's sweep rows (ee-scan-to-seos.mjs) and folded
//                  into a copy of the answers (merge-sweep.mjs). Repeatable. Note: the converter stamps the rows' read_at
//                  with the export's file time, which reaches market.json and report-data.json (run-log.txt records it).
//   --facts        the independent facts file for this business (extract-v2.mjs --facts); Green Haven only today.
//   --no-browser   skip conformance/check-documents.mjs (headless Chrome).
// Read from the answers, not typed: the store's place id and state (the business answer's first location row). The time
// zone is settings.timezone, else the state table read out of reference/extract-v2.mjs (one table, never a second copy).
// The searches the owner expects (sweeps-market --want) are settings.expected_searches.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REF = path.join(HERE, 'reference');
const CHECK_DOCS = path.join(HERE, 'conformance', 'check-documents.mjs');
const USAGE = 'usage: node run-report.mjs --data=<folder> --settings=<file> --out=<folder> [--extra-sweep=<Eagle Eyes export>]... [--facts=<file>] [--no-browser]';
const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
const KNOWN = ['--data=', '--settings=', '--out=', '--extra-sweep=', '--facts=', '--no-browser'];
const stop = (m, code = 1) => { console.error('RUN STOPPED: ' + m); process.exit(code); };
const unknown = argv.filter(a => !KNOWN.some(k => k.endsWith('=') ? a.startsWith(k) : a === k));
if (unknown.length) stop(`unknown argument${unknown.length > 1 ? 's' : ''}: ${unknown.join(' ')}\n${USAGE}`, 2);
const opt = k => { const a = argv.find(v => v.startsWith('--' + k + '=')); return a ? a.slice(k.length + 3) : null; };
const many = k => argv.filter(v => v.startsWith('--' + k + '=')).map(v => v.slice(k.length + 3));
if (!opt('data') || !opt('settings') || !opt('out')) stop(USAGE, 2);
const DATA = path.resolve(opt('data')), SETTINGS = path.resolve(opt('settings')), OUT = path.resolve(opt('out'));
const EXTRA = many('extra-sweep').map(p => path.resolve(p)), FACTS = opt('facts') ? path.resolve(opt('facts')) : null, BROWSER = !argv.includes('--no-browser');
const sha = b => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');

// ---------- the inputs ----------
if (!fs.existsSync(DATA) || !fs.statSync(DATA).isDirectory()) stop('no data folder at ' + DATA);
for (const [p, what] of [[SETTINGS, 'settings file'], ...EXTRA.map(p => [p, 'Eagle Eyes export']), ...(FACTS ? [[FACTS, 'facts file']] : [])]) if (!fs.existsSync(p) || !fs.statSync(p).isFile()) stop(`no ${what} at ${p}`);
let settings; try { settings = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(SETTINGS, 'utf8')); } catch (e) { stop(`the settings file is not JSON: ${e.message}`); }
const ID = settings.business_id;
if (!Number.isInteger(ID)) stop('settings.business_id is required (the SEOS business id the answers are about)');
const FILES = { biz: `business-${ID}.json`, full: `full-audit-${ID}.json`, web: `website-audit-${ID}.json` };
const GETS = { biz: `/businesses/${ID}`, full: `/businesses/${ID}/full-audit-result`, web: `/businesses/${ID}/website-audit-result` };
for (const k of Object.keys(FILES)) if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(DATA, FILES[k]))) stop(`missing ${FILES[k]} in ${DATA} (SEOS's answer to GET ${GETS[k]})`);
let biz; try { biz = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(DATA, FILES.biz), 'utf8')); } catch (e) { stop(`${FILES.biz} is not JSON: ${e.message}`); }
if ((biz.business_id ?? biz.tables?.businesses?.[0]?.id) !== ID) stop(`${FILES.biz} is about business ${biz.business_id ?? biz.tables?.businesses?.[0]?.id}, the settings about ${ID}`);
const loc = biz.tables?.locations?.[0] || stop(`${FILES.biz} has no location row`);
const PID = loc.place_id || stop(`the location row in ${FILES.biz} has no place id`);
// the state table, read out of the extractor itself so the two can never drift apart
const tzTable = () => {
  const src = fs.readFileSync(path.join(REF, 'extract-v2.mjs'), 'utf8');
  const m = /const TZ = \{([^}]*)\};/.exec(src) || stop('could not find the state table (const TZ = {...};) in reference/extract-v2.mjs');
  const pairs = [...m[1].matchAll(/([A-Z]{2}): '([^']+)'/g)], items = m[1].split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  if (pairs.length !== items.length) stop(`the state table in reference/extract-v2.mjs has ${items.length} entries and ${pairs.length} read as STATE: 'Zone'`);
  return Object.fromEntries(pairs.map(p => [p[1], p[2]]));
};
const TZ = settings.timezone || tzTable()[loc.state] || stop(`no time zone for state ${loc.state}: give settings.timezone`);
try { new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone: TZ }); } catch { stop(`${settings.timezone ? 'settings.timezone' : 'the state table'} gives "${TZ}", which is not a time zone`); }
const want = Array.isArray(settings.expected_searches) ? settings.expected_searches.map(s => String(s).trim()).filter(Boolean) : [];
if (want.some(s => s.includes(','))) stop('an expected search holds a comma, which sweeps-market.mjs --want reads as a separator');

if (fs.existsSync(OUT) && fs.readdirSync(OUT).length) stop('the out folder is not empty: ' + OUT);
fs.mkdirSync(path.join(OUT, 'logs'), { recursive: true });

// ---------- the stages ----------
const log = [], started = Date.now();
const header = [`run-report.mjs`, `data: ${DATA}`, `settings: ${SETTINGS} (sha256 ${sha(fs.readFileSync(SETTINGS))})`, `business ${ID}, store place id ${PID}, state ${loc.state}, time zone ${TZ}${settings.timezone ? ' (settings)' : ' (state table in reference/extract-v2.mjs)'}`,
  `expected searches: ${want.length ? want.map(s => `"${s}"`).join(', ') : 'none'}`, ...EXTRA.map(p => `extra sweep: ${p} (sha256 ${sha(fs.readFileSync(p))}, file time ${fs.statSync(p).mtime.toISOString()}: ee-scan-to-seos.mjs stamps read_at with it)`),
  `facts: ${FACTS ? `${FACTS} (sha256 ${sha(fs.readFileSync(FACTS))})` : 'none'}`, `browser check: ${BROWSER ? 'yes' : 'no (--no-browser)'}`, ''];
const writeLog = status => fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, 'run-log.txt'), [...header, 'stage\texit\tseconds\tcommand', ...log.map(r => `${r.stage}\t${r.exit}\t${r.seconds}\t${r.command}`), '', status, ''].join('\n'));
const run = (stage, script, args) => {
  const t0 = Date.now();
  const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, [script, ...args], { cwd: OUT, encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 1 << 28 });
  const seconds = ((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1), exit = r.status === null ? `signal ${r.signal}` : r.status;
  const quote = a => (/[\s"]/.test(a) ? JSON.stringify(a) : a);
  log.push({ stage, exit, seconds, command: ['node', script, ...args].map(quote).join(' ') });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, 'logs', `${String(log.length).padStart(2, '0')}-${stage.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gi, '-')}.log`), `$ ${log[log.length - 1].command}\n--- stdout\n${r.stdout || ''}\n--- stderr\n${r.stderr || ''}\n--- exit ${exit}\n`);
  if (r.error) { writeLog(`STOPPED at ${stage}: ${r.error.message}`); stop(`${stage} could not start: ${r.error.message}`); }
  if (r.status !== 0) {
    const tail = (r.stderr || '').trim() || (r.stdout || '').trim();
    writeLog(`STOPPED at ${stage} (exit ${exit})`);
    console.error(`RUN STOPPED at ${stage} (exit ${exit})\n` + tail.split('\n').slice(-15).map(l => '  ' + l).join('\n'));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log(`${stage.padEnd(24)} ok  ${seconds}s`);
  return r.stdout;
};
const ref = f => path.join(REF, f);

// 1. each Eagle Eyes export: converted, then folded into a copy of the answers (the last copy is <out>/data)
let D = DATA;
EXTRA.forEach((x, i) => {
  const n = EXTRA.length > 1 ? `[${i + 1}]` : '';
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(OUT, 'extra'), { recursive: true });
  const conv = path.join(OUT, 'extra', path.basename(x).replace(/\.json$/i, '') + '.seos.json');
  run('ee-scan-to-seos' + n, ref('ee-scan-to-seos.mjs'), [x, PID, conv]);
  const next = i === EXTRA.length - 1 ? path.join(OUT, 'data') : path.join(OUT, `data-merge-${i + 1}`);
  run('merge-sweep' + n, ref('merge-sweep.mjs'), [D, conv, next]);
  D = next;
});
const IN = k => path.join(D, FILES[k]);
const ALL_SWEEPS = path.join(D, 'engine_sweeps-all.json'), LOCATIONS = path.join(D, 'locations-all.json');
const hasAll = fs.existsSync(ALL_SWEEPS), hasLoc = fs.existsSync(LOCATIONS);
const O = f => path.join(OUT, f);

// 2. the market file from the store's sweeps, and its second reading
run('sweeps-market', ref('sweeps-market.mjs'), [IN('biz'), IN('full'), PID, O('market.json'), `--tz=${TZ}`, ...(hasAll ? [`--all-sweeps=${ALL_SWEEPS}`] : []), ...(want.length ? [`--want=${want.join(',')}`] : [])]);
run('check-sweeps-market', ref('check-sweeps-market.mjs'), [IN('biz'), O('market.json'), `--audit=${IN('full')}`]);

// 3. the report model, and its second reading
run('extract-v2', ref('extract-v2.mjs'), [IN('biz'), IN('full'), IN('web'), O('report-data.json'), `--settings=${SETTINGS}`, `--market=${O('market.json')}`,
  ...(hasAll ? [`--all-sweeps=${ALL_SWEEPS}`] : []), ...(hasLoc ? [`--locations=${LOCATIONS}`] : []), ...(FACTS ? [`--facts=${FACTS}`] : [])]);
{ const m = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(O('market.json'), 'utf8')), d = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(O('report-data.json'), 'utf8'));
  if (d.meta?.v2 !== true) { writeLog('STOPPED: report-data.json is not v2 data'); stop('report-data.json is not v2 data (meta.v2)'); }
  if (m.tz !== TZ || d.meta.timezone !== TZ) { writeLog('STOPPED: two time zones'); stop(`two time zones in one report: the market file ${m.tz}, the model ${d.meta.timezone}, the run ${TZ}`); } }
run('check-compare-v2', ref('check-compare-v2.mjs'), [IN('biz'), IN('full'), IN('web'), O('report-data.json')]);

// 4. the two documents, and their checks
run('build-report client', ref('build-report.mjs'), [O('report-data.json'), O('competitor-analysis.html'), '--audience=client', '--doc=Competitor Analysis']);
run('build-report service', ref('build-report.mjs'), [O('report-data.json'), O('action-plan.html'), '--audience=service', '--doc=Action Plan']);
run('verify-classes client', ref('verify-classes.mjs'), [O('competitor-analysis.html')]);
run('verify-classes service', ref('verify-classes.mjs'), [O('action-plan.html')]);
if (BROWSER) run('check-documents', CHECK_DOCS, [O('report-data.json'), O('competitor-analysis.html'), O('action-plan.html'), O('screenshots')]);

// 5. the record
const OUTPUTS = ['market.json', 'report-data.json', 'competitor-analysis.html', 'action-plan.html'];
fs.writeFileSync(O('SHA256SUMS'), OUTPUTS.map(f => `${sha(fs.readFileSync(O(f)))}  ${f}`).join('\n') + '\n');
writeLog(`DONE in ${((Date.now() - started) / 1000).toFixed(1)}s: ${OUTPUTS.join(', ')}`);

// conformance.mjs: same SEOS data in, same two documents out. Checks the reference chain (or a port of it) against the
// Green Haven fixture's expected outputs (fixtures/green-haven-48/expected/).
//
// usage:
//   node conformance.mjs [--no-browser] [--keep]
//       runs run-report.mjs on fixtures/green-haven-48 (scrubbed input, settings.json, the Eagle Eyes export as
//       --extra-sweep, --facts=oracle/gh-facts.json) into a fresh folder under the system temp folder, then compares:
//       market.json and both documents byte for byte, report-data.json deep-equal apart from meta.built_at.
//       Exit 0 only when all of it holds. The temp folder is removed on a pass (kept with --keep, always kept on a fail).
//   node conformance.mjs --model=<report-data.json>
//       a port's model against expected/report-data.json, deep-equal apart from meta.built_at and meta.facts_check (the
//       record of the Green Haven facts check, which only extract-v2.mjs --facts writes; a port need not port that check);
//       prints every differing path.
//   node conformance.mjs --documents=<folder>
//       a port's competitor-analysis.html and action-plan.html against expected/, byte for byte; on a difference prints
//       the first differing offset with 120 characters of context.
//   node conformance.mjs --write-expected
//       (owner only, after a reviewed change to reference/) writes expected/ from a fresh run. Refuses when expected/
//       already holds files: delete them first, on purpose.
// The Eagle Eyes export's file time is pinned from fixture.json before the run: ee-scan-to-seos.mjs stamps the sweep's
// read_at with it, and market.json and report-data.json carry read_at, so an unpinned copy would fail on another machine.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const PKG = path.resolve(HERE, '..');
const FX = path.join(PKG, 'fixtures', 'green-haven-48');
const EXP = path.join(FX, 'expected');
const OUTPUTS = ['market.json', 'report-data.json', 'competitor-analysis.html', 'action-plan.html'];
const DOCS = ['competitor-analysis.html', 'action-plan.html'];
const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
const opt = k => { const a = argv.find(v => v.startsWith('--' + k + '=')); return a ? a.slice(k.length + 3) : null; };
const flag = k => argv.includes('--' + k);
const sha = b => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');
const stop = m => { console.error('CONFORMANCE STOPPED: ' + m); process.exit(2); };

// ---------- comparisons ----------
// every path where two JSON values differ, meta.built_at left out (the one clock read of the extraction); with --model also
// meta.facts_check (the fixture run writes it with --facts; a port's model has no reason to)
const SKIP = new Set(['meta.built_at', ...(opt('model') ? ['meta.facts_check'] : [])]);
const jsonDiff = (want, got) => {
  const out = [];
  const show = v => { const s = JSON.stringify(v); return s === undefined ? '(absent)' : s.length > 160 ? s.slice(0, 160) + '...' : s; };
  const walk = (a, b, p) => {
    if (SKIP.has(p)) return;
    if (a && b && typeof a === 'object' && typeof b === 'object' && Array.isArray(a) === Array.isArray(b)) {
      if (Array.isArray(a)) { if (a.length !== b.length) out.push(`${p}: ${a.length} items expected, ${b.length} found`); for (let i = 0; i < Math.max(a.length, b.length); i++) walk(a[i], b[i], `${p}[${i}]`); }
      else for (const k of [...new Set([...Object.keys(a), ...Object.keys(b)])]) walk(a[k], b[k], p ? `${p}.${k}` : k);
      return;
    }
    if (JSON.stringify(a) !== JSON.stringify(b)) out.push(`${p || '(root)'}: expected ${show(a)}, found ${show(b)}`);
  };
  walk(want, got, '');
  return out;
};
const firstDiff = (want, got) => { const n = Math.min(want.length, got.length); let i = 0; while (i < n && want[i] === got[i]) i++; return i === n && want.length === got.length ? -1 : i; };
const context = (buf, i) => JSON.stringify(buf.subarray(Math.max(0, i - 60), i + 60).toString('utf8'));
const compareBytes = (name, wantPath, gotPath) => {
  if (!fs.existsSync(gotPath)) return [`${name}: not found at ${gotPath}`];
  const want = fs.readFileSync(wantPath), got = fs.readFileSync(gotPath);
  if (want.equals(got)) return [];
  const i = firstDiff(want, got);
  return [`${name}: differs (${want.length} bytes expected, ${got.length} found); first difference at byte ${i}\n    expected ${context(want, i)}\n    found    ${context(got, i)}`];
};
const compareModel = gotPath => {
  if (!fs.existsSync(gotPath)) return [`report-data.json: not found at ${gotPath}`];
  let got; try { got = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(gotPath, 'utf8')); } catch (e) { return [`report-data.json: not JSON (${e.message})`]; }
  return jsonDiff(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(EXP, 'report-data.json'), 'utf8')), got).map(d => 'report-data.json ' + d);
};
const expectedIntact = () => {
  const sums = path.join(EXP, 'SHA256SUMS'); if (!fs.existsSync(sums)) stop('expected/SHA256SUMS is missing');
  const bad = fs.readFileSync(sums, 'utf8').trim().split('\n').map(l => l.split(/\s+/)).filter(([h, f]) => !fs.existsSync(path.join(EXP, f)) || sha(fs.readFileSync(path.join(EXP, f))) !== h).map(([, f]) => f);
  if (bad.length) stop('expected/ does not match its SHA256SUMS: ' + bad.join(', '));
};
const report = (problems, label, t0) => {
  for (const p of problems) console.log('  ' + p);
  const secs = t0 ? ` in ${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1)}s` : '';
  console.log(problems.length ? `CONFORMANCE: FAIL (${label}: ${problems.length} difference${problems.length === 1 ? '' : 's'})${secs}` : `CONFORMANCE: PASS (${label})${secs}`);
  return problems.length ? 1 : 0;
};

// ---------- a port's model or documents ----------
if (opt('model')) { expectedIntact(); process.exit(report(compareModel(path.resolve(opt('model'))), 'model against expected/report-data.json, apart from meta.built_at and meta.facts_check')); }
if (opt('documents')) { expectedIntact(); const dir = path.resolve(opt('documents')); process.exit(report(DOCS.flatMap(f => compareBytes(f, path.join(EXP, f), path.join(dir, f))), 'documents against expected/, byte for byte')); }

// ---------- the reference chain on the fixture ----------
const WRITE = flag('write-expected');
if (WRITE && fs.existsSync(EXP) && fs.readdirSync(EXP).length) stop('expected/ already holds files; delete them first if the reference really changed');
if (!WRITE) expectedIntact();
const fixture = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(FX, 'fixture.json'), 'utf8'));
const t0 = Date.now();
const tmp = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'seos-conformance-'));
const extras = (fixture.extra_sweeps || []).map(x => {
  const src = path.join(FX, x.file), dst = path.join(tmp, 'extra', path.basename(x.file));
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(dst), { recursive: true }); fs.copyFileSync(src, dst);
  if (sha(fs.readFileSync(dst)) !== x.sha256) stop(`${x.file} is not the file fixture.json records`);
  const t = new Date(x.mtime); fs.utimesSync(dst, t, t);
  if (fs.statSync(dst).mtime.toISOString() !== x.mtime) stop(`this file system cannot hold the export's file time ${x.mtime} (it reads back ${fs.statSync(dst).mtime.toISOString()})`);
  return dst;
});
const args = [path.join(PKG, 'run-report.mjs'), `--data=${path.join(FX, 'input')}`, `--settings=${path.join(FX, 'settings.json')}`, `--out=${path.join(tmp, 'out')}`,
  ...extras.map(x => `--extra-sweep=${x}`), `--facts=${path.join(FX, 'oracle', 'gh-facts.json')}`, ...(flag('no-browser') ? ['--no-browser'] : [])];
console.log(`conformance: run-report.mjs on fixtures/green-haven-48 into ${tmp}`);
const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, args, { stdio: 'inherit' });
const OUT = path.join(tmp, 'out');
if (r.status !== 0) { console.log(`  run-report.mjs exited ${r.status}; the run is kept in ${tmp}`); process.exit(report(['run-report.mjs did not finish'], 'the fixture run', t0)); }
if (WRITE) {
  fs.mkdirSync(EXP, { recursive: true });
  for (const f of OUTPUTS) fs.copyFileSync(path.join(OUT, f), path.join(EXP, f));
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(EXP, 'SHA256SUMS'), OUTPUTS.map(f => `${sha(fs.readFileSync(path.join(EXP, f)))}  ${f}`).join('\n') + '\n');
  console.log(`wrote expected/ (${OUTPUTS.join(', ')}, SHA256SUMS) from ${OUT}`);
  if (!flag('keep')) fs.rmSync(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
  process.exit(0);
}
const problems = [
  ...compareBytes('market.json', path.join(EXP, 'market.json'), path.join(OUT, 'market.json')),
  ...DOCS.flatMap(f => compareBytes(f, path.join(EXP, f), path.join(OUT, f))),
  ...compareModel(path.join(OUT, 'report-data.json')),
];
const code = report(problems, 'the fixture run: market.json and both documents byte for byte, report-data.json apart from meta.built_at', t0);
if (code || flag('keep')) console.log(`  the run is kept in ${tmp}`); else fs.rmSync(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
process.exit(code);

Builders' reports

Who built what, and what changed after

parts/README.md 3 KB

The builders' reports

Four agents built this package's parts on 2026-10-12, in parallel, each from the reference code and the Green Haven data. These are their reports as they returned them. One edit: in B-contract.json the absolute paths into our working tree were cut to start at the repository folder (Product/seos-report/...), so they no longer carry our machine's folder names; read every path in these reports as relative to our repository, mapped to this package by SPEC.md section 13.

FilePartHolds
A-build.jsonrunner, fixture, conformance, variantsevery file, check and result; the scrub record; the runner's stages and failure tests; 21 findings; 8 unverified points
B-contract.jsoninputs, settings, modelhow each contract file was generated; 14 checks; counts; 26 findings; 10 unverified points
C1-outline.jsonoutline and wordinghow to run the checkers; 9 checks; 27 findings; 6 unverified points
C2-rules.jsonruleswhat was read; 10 checks; counts; 19 findings; 8 unverified points

OPEN-ITEMS.md merges the 93 findings (many were found by more than one part) into one list.

What changed after these reports

Two changes were made to the fixture after them, during assembly (fixtures/green-haven-48/scrub.mjs, input/SCRUBBED.md):

  • the SEOS console users' e-mail addresses (2 addresses, held as whole values in 973 fields across 5 input files) were replaced by person-<n>@example.invalid. Part A had left them in and flagged them for a decision;
  • after the independent check, the Eagle Eyes export's request.vantage.ip and .isp (the scan machine's network address and provider) were set to null. Nothing in the chain reads them: every output came out byte-identical, and expected/ did not change.

Effects, measured:

  • The two expected documents did not change (byte-identical to the live Green Haven documents before and after).
  • expected/market.json and expected/report-data.json changed only where they record the input files' size and sha256 (5 and 13 paths). Conformance passed on the new fixture; the variants' results and VARIANTS.md came out byte-identical.
  • So the sha256 values that A-build.json gives for the fixture's input files (fixture.input_files, the Eagle Eyes export's included), for expected/market.json and expected/report-data.json (conformance.expected) and in its scrub record are those of the fixture before these changes. The current values are in fixtures/green-haven-48/fixture.json, fixtures/green-haven-48/expected/SHA256SUMS and MANIFEST.json. The documents' values in A-build.json still hold.
  • A-build.json's note that the e-mail addresses are "the owner's call" is settled by this change.
